title: Visit Qatar hosts Audi Revolut F1 Team drivers for a cultural tour and fan event in Doha
article_text:
Doha, Qatar: As Principal Partner of Audi Revolut F1 Team, Visit Qatar hosted team drivers Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto in Doha on 25 November, ahead of the Formula 1® Qatar Airways Qatar Grand Prix.

During their visit, the drivers explored some of Doha’s best-known cultural and urban destinations, including Souq Waqif, Msheireb Downtown Doha and the Museum of Islamic Art (MIA), offering an opportunity to experience Qatar’s heritage, architecture and contemporary identity.

The programme also featured an engagement event at Crystal Walk, Gewan Island, showcasing the team’s show car with bespoke Visit Qatar pattern details, alongside an interactive Q&A session with both drivers.

The Doha activation marks the third initiative delivered by Visit Qatar through its partnership with the team this season. Previous activations included ‘La Parada’ in Madrid, a three-day public activation held at Plaza de Santiago from 9 to 11 September, and ‘The Garden Souq by Visit Qatar’ in Singapore, which welcomed more than 1,700 visitors at Raffles Hotel Singapore from 7 to 9 October.

Through its partnership with Audi Revolut F1 Team, Visit Qatar is extending the destination’s international reach by connecting with global audiences through one of the world’s most prominent sporting platforms. The activations provide opportunities to showcase Qatar’s cultural attractions, hospitality and visitor experiences across key international markets, while bringing the destination closer to motorsport fans.

title: Standard Chartered and F1 ACADEMY Launch 'Drive Further' Financial Skills Initiative
article_text:
Standard Chartered has partnered with F1 ACADEMY to launch ‘Drive Further,’ a multi-year financial literacy initiative for female racing drivers. By providing training in sponsorship, budgeting, and investment, the programme addresses the commercial complexities of professional motorsport, ensuring athletes possess the financial acumen required to manage their careers as effectively as their performance on the track.

The "Drive Further" initiative is a multi-year programme designed to equip female drivers with the practical financial and commercial skills necessary to sustain a career in professional motorsport. Developed in response to needs identified by the drivers themselves, the curriculum focuses on areas where young athletes often face significant pressure, including sponsorship acquisition, financial planning, budgeting, and investment strategies. The programme combines virtual learning modules with in-person workshops and personalised support, leveraging the banking and wealth management expertise of Standard Chartered.

Throughout 2026, the initiative has already delivered training sessions featuring senior figures such as Steve Brice, Global Chief Investment Officer at Standard Chartered, who shared insights directly with the driver cohort. A key component of the rollout included an in-person workshop conducted on the sidelines of the Formula 1 MSC Cruises United States Grand Prix 2026 in Austin. By integrating these financial modules into the F1 ACADEMY calendar, the partnership aims to bridge the gap between on-track performance and the business realities of the sport. Standard Chartered and F1 ACADEMY intend to evolve the programme in the coming years through close collaboration with each new cohort of drivers, ensuring the curriculum remains responsive to the shifting commercial landscape of global racing.

"Building a career in motorsport extends beyond performance on the track. Through Drive Further, we’re bringing together our banking and wealth management expertise to help young female drivers navigate the financial and commercial aspects of their careers. By supporting them early in their journey, we’re enabling them to seize new opportunities and move ahead with confidence."

Judy Hsu, CEO, Wealth & Retail Banking, Standard Chartered.

Standard Chartered is a leading international banking group with a significant presence in the world’s most dynamic markets, particularly across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. The bank has increasingly focused on expanding its Wealth and Retail Banking division, positioning itself as a specialist in navigating complex global financial landscapes for high-net-worth individuals and emerging talent. In recent years, the institution has leveraged high-profile sports partnerships to champion diversity and inclusion, aligning its corporate social responsibility goals with its commercial expertise. F1 ACADEMY is an ambitious all-female racing series established by Formula 1 to develop and prepare young drivers for higher levels of competition. The series serves as a critical pipeline for female talent in a historically male-dominated industry, providing the track time, testing, and technical support required to progress through the motorsport ladder. By partnering with a global financial institution, the academy acknowledges that technical driving skill must be matched by commercial literacy to ensure long-term career viability.

FF News has extensively tracked Standard Chartered’s strategic pivot toward digital assets and specialised wealth services. The bank recently made headlines when Standard Chartered to Acquire Zodia Custody in Major Digital Asset Expansion was announced, signaling a significant move into the institutional crypto space. This followed the launch of Standard Chartered Launches First-of-its-Kind Crypto Trading for Wealth Clients in UAE, further cementing its position in the Middle Eastern wealth market. Leadership changes have also been a focus, including the news that Standard Chartered Names Ying Ying Tan as Global Head of Securities Services and Digital Assets. Additionally, the bank’s ecosystem continues to evolve with the appointment of Jan Brzezek as CEO of Zodia Markets, as reported in Zodia Markets Appoints Crypto Finance AG Founder Jan Brzezek as CEO.

This partnership highlights a growing trend where financial institutions move beyond traditional logo-on-car sponsorships toward "value-add" educational partnerships. For the fintech and banking sector, this move signals an attempt to capture the next generation of high-net-worth individuals—athletes—at the very start of their earning potential. It puts pressure on other retail banks to demonstrate how their expertise applies to specific, high-risk career paths rather than offering generic financial advice. The initiative raises broader questions for the industry about the role of banks in athlete management and whether financial literacy will become a standard component of professional sports development moving forward.

Standard Chartered and F1 ACADEMY™ have today launched ‘Drive Further’, a multi-year financial skills initiative designed to give female drivers the knowledge, confidence and practical skills to navigate the financial and commercial decisions that come with building a career in motorsport.

While talent and performance are fundamental to success on the track, building a career in motorsport requires drivers to navigate a complex financial and commercial landscape. Access to the right skills, networks and development opportunities can therefore play an important role in helping young female driving talent progress. Drive Further has been developed to support in these areas while reflecting the needs identified by the drivers themselves.

Building on the strength of the partnership between Standard Chartered and F1 ACADEMY™, the Drive Further initiative brings together the all-female series’ commitment to developing drivers with Standard Chartered’s ambition to use its expertise and network to help talented young women realise their potential.

"Building a career in motorsport extends beyond performance on the track. Through Drive Further, we’re bringing together our banking and wealth management expertise to help young female drivers navigate the financial and commercial aspects of their careers. By supporting them early in their journey, we’re enabling them to seize new opportunities and move ahead with confidence." said Judy Hsu, CEO, Wealth & Retail Banking, Standard Chartered.

title: LFP secures key court ruling to deploy real-time piracy blocking
article_text:
The LFP, domestic French soccer’s organizing body, has secured a court ruling allowing it to block pirate services during broadcasts of top-flight Ligue 1 and second-tier Ligue 2 matches automatically and in real-time.

The ruling allows internet service providers to block illegal streams under new anti-piracy legislation introduced in August.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The Paris Judicial Court issued its ruling on November 20, becoming the first to authorise the new blocking mechanism established by France’s law of August 3, 2026, on the organisation and financing of professional sport.

This decision paves the way for the deployment of an automated system that will allow the LFP to identify and block pirate streaming services as they emerge during live Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 matches.

With this development, the LFP will no longer have to rely on the existing process of weekly updates and manual approval by French audiovisual regulator Arcom.

An automated system is expected to become operational in the coming weeks, enabling internet service providers to implement blocking orders without delay, under Arcom’s supervision.

Court rulings obtained by the league last July already allowed for the protection of LFP competitions against pirate services throughout the 2026-2027 season.

In a statement, the LFP said: “This judgment, issued within the framework of the proceedings initiated by the LFP Group against internet service providers to obtain the right to block pirate services in real time, marks a new step.

“For the first time, the LFP Group will be able to rely on the mechanism established by the law of August 3, 2026, to act at the very moment new pirate services appear during the broadcast of matches.

“The automated system necessary for its implementation is expected to be deployed in the coming weeks, under the control of Arcom, in order to allow Internet service providers to implement the ordered blocks without delay.”

Through the new system, the French league body is seeking to “minimize the time between identifying a pirate service and blocking it, in order to prevent access at the very moment when the damage is greatest, during the broadcast of matches.”

The LFP believes the new mechanism will allow it to “significantly increase the speed and effectiveness of its action against piracy and strengthen the protection of its competitions, its broadcasters, and the revenues of professional football.”

The organization added: “The fight against piracy is a major challenge for the professional football economy.

“Protecting content at the very moment it is broadcast means protecting the value of audiovisual rights, the investments made by broadcasters, and the revenue that allows clubs to grow. With this new system, the LFP Group is strengthening its ability to defend one of its most strategic assets.”

The move could boost the LFP’s attempt to secure new domestic broadcast partners after recently launching a tender process.

The tender covers five seasons from the 2027-28 through 2031-32 cycle and represents a U-turn by the body after it originally planned to keep the current broadcast arrangement through 2028-29.

The process went live on November 3 and will run until 3 December, after which bids will be examined the LFP and its LFP Media arm.

The tender contains a single package for all Ligue 1 games each season – as is now permitted under French competition law – as well as the exclusive distribution of Ligue 1+, the league’s OTT streaming platform.

Should a traditional linear broadcaster or streaming service secure the main package of rights, it could spell the end of the road for Ligue 1+, which was launched – mostly out of necessity – in mid-2025, and covered all games from the 18-team Ligue 1 last season.

Ligue 1+ exclusively held the rights to eight of the league’s nine weekly games last season and aired the ninth game (a BeIN exclusive live fixture) on a delay.

The establishment of the in-house platform followed the premature termination of a previous domestic rights agreement between the LFP and global subscription service DAZN.

Ligue 1's domestic media rights have been a source of turmoil and significant concern for the LFP for the last seven years, during which time they have decreased in value significantly.

title: Argentina bans online betting by minors, gambling sponsorships
article_text:
Argentina's Senate has unanimously passed legislation banning minors from online gambling and prohibiting betting companies from advertising, promoting or sponsoring gambling on sports kits, a move aimed at tackling gambling addiction among young people.

The bill passed with 72 votes in favour, both in the general vote and on individual articles, following an agreement between the ruling La Libertad Avanza (LLA) party and the Peronist opposition.

The legislation had been stalled for more than two years and was close to losing parliamentary status before renewed pressure from the Catholic Church. The recent visit by Pope Leo XIV to Argentina helped bring it back to the agenda.

President Javier government had sought to approve an amended version of the bill focused on combating illegal gambling, but opposed sweeping restrictions on advertising, a position also backed by the Argentine Football Association (AFA) and several top clubs that receive large amounts of sponsorship money from betting companies.

The law's central provisions prevent minors from betting on digital platforms and prohibit advertising, promotion and sponsorship of gambling and online betting.

The restrictions extend to the Internet, social media, information and communications technology, audiovisual media and outdoor advertising.

Betting company sponsorship of sports kits is also banned, as is advertising in print, radio, television and other existing or future communications platforms.

Advertising will only be permitted inside casinos, bingo halls, racecourses, betting venues and lottery agencies.

The legislation also establishes prison sentences of between three and eight years for those who organise or operate gambling systems without authorisation from the relevant jurisdiction.

It introduces a series of preventive measures, including a self-exclusion register, identity checks using facial recognition, restrictions on payment methods and alerts notifying users of the time and money they spend gambling.

One of the bill's sponsors, ruling La Libertad Avanza party lawmaker Agustín Coto, said: "If we pass this law today, I want people to understand that we are not here to morally police anyone. This is not about who is good or bad, but about public health. There is a limit, and that limit is children."

Catamarca Peronist Senator Lucía Corpacci said the public was demanding an urgent response, describing the legislation as the most comprehensive of the bills they had introduced on the issue.

"We need to pass this law. Although the provinces regulate gambling, we are now talking about a different kind of game," she said.

She warned that online betting had become part of everyday life for many minors, who gamble from their living rooms, bedrooms and even schools.

"We are talking about gambling from the living room of a house, from a child's bedroom or even from school, because online betting is part of the everyday reality of many minors who gamble at school," she added.

Ruling party Senate leader Patricia Bullrich shared the testimony of the mother of a 26-year-old man who had reached breaking point because of gambling addiction and debts.

"No child or family can keep waiting for the pace of politics. This law must be passed today," she wrote in a post on social media.

Closing the debate, Peronist bloc leader José Mayans welcomed the agreement between the parties and said passing the bill unanimously would be a positive signal.

"I think it is very good that we can pass this unanimously," he said, praising Congress for taking up the issue again, rather than allowing it to be postponed once more.

Bullrich even proposed naming the legislation the "Pope Leo XIV Law" in recognition of the impetus the issue had received, though she stressed that families and schools have a role in tackling gambling addiction.

Church leaders welcomed the bill's passage in a statement, writing: "This achievement does not belong to any particular sector: it is a collective triumph for all of Argentine society.”

The law will force the domestic football authorities to rip up its commercial arrangements, with clubs including Boca Juniors and River Plate set to face large financial blows.

The restrictions cover betting company logos on shirts as well as advertising at stadiums, in public spaces and on clubs' social media channels.

Boca and River both have betting sponsors on their official club kits, while the AFA and domestic top flight will also have to adapt their commercial agreements and advertising.

Although Argentina's national team does not wear betting company sponsors on its shirts, such brands feature across its digital channels, press conference banners and television advertising.

Betting companies are among the main shirt sponsors of clubs including Boca, River, Independiente, Racing, San Lorenzo, Huracán, Rosario Central and Newell's, among other clubs.

Boca and River have the two biggest betting sponsorship deals in Argentine football, both running until 2028, which will have to be renegotiated.

The restrictions will also extend to footballers, coaches, former players, referees, sports journalists and influencers, who will no longer be allowed to feature in betting advertising campaigns, promote sites or share promotional codes through media or social networks.

Many national team stars, including goalkeeper Emiliano 'Dibu' Martínez, have advertised betting firms.

Broadcasters showing matches in the Primera División and lower divisions will also have to remove betting adverts during games and from their regular programming.

title: River and Loma Negra: Sponsorship Agreement as Part of the Monumental Expansion and Roofing
article_text:
The leading company in the construction industry became the official sponsor of the Club until 2030, under an agreement that includes the provision of concrete for the expansion and roofing works of the Stadium.

River Plate and Loma Negra announced the signing of a sponsorship agreement through which the cement company will be a strategic supplier for the expansion and roofing works of the Monumental Stadium by providing concrete, thus becoming the official sponsor of the Club until 2030.

The initiative brings together two centenarian Argentine institutions, protagonists of their respective activities and united by a trajectory built on passion, work, and the constant pursuit of excellence. Loma Negra will contribute its experience, technical capacity, and solutions for the construction of an emblematic project for River, its members, and fans.

The agreement includes brand presence in the Club's official spaces and channels, including the Monumental Stadium, River Camp, press conferences, digital content, and social networks. It will also develop activations and experiences aimed at clients and other audiences related to Loma Negra.

Additionally, it foresees pre-match experiences and interactions with the professional squad, visits to training sessions, exclusive tours of the River Museum, corporate events at the Club's facilities, and various actions during local tournament matches.

Stefano Di Carlo stated: “Adding Loma Negra as an Official Sponsor represents a very important step to continue driving the transformation of the Monumental. Their experience and leadership in the construction industry will be fundamental to accompany this new challenge and continue consolidating a stadium prepared to welcome millions of people each year.”

In turn, Sergio Faifman (CEO of Loma Negra) noted: “This project brings together two centenarian institutions, deeply connected with the country and with a history marked by growth, innovation, and the ability to build projects that leave a mark.”

Loma Negra is the leading company in the Argentine cement industry and celebrates 100 years in 2026 as a protagonist in the construction of the country. Since its inception in Olavarría in 1926, the company has developed an integrated business and a wide productive and logistical network that allows it to reach the main markets in Argentina.

It produces and markets cement, masonry cement, lime, concrete, and aggregates, providing solutions for distributors, concrete producers, industrial clients, and large infrastructure projects.

Its trajectory is based on innovation, operational excellence, and the constant pursuit of sustainable solutions. Through its products, services, and technical capacity, Loma Negra supports the development of works that transform communities and contribute to the country's growth.

title: Generali expands World Tennis partnership to grassroots programs
article_text:
The World Tennis governing body has extended and expanded its partnership with Generali Group just months after the international insurance company became the title sponsor of the major Davis Cup tournament.

This new grassroots-focused agreement will see the pair collaborate on a number of programs focused on increasing tennis uptake globally among target demographics.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In all, five programs will be supported throughout the agreement: the Generali World Tennis Masters Tour (a seniors series for players over the age of 30), the Generali Junior Tennis Initiative (a grassroots tennis education program), Generali Coaches For Life (coaching education program), Generali World Tennis Activation (local mass participation events centered around Davis Cup matchups), and Generali Rally Together Fund (money ringfenced for new tennis infrastructure globally).

This deal, with multi-year agreement, includes “significant investment” and has an aim of bringing as many a 1 million new young people into tennis.

World Tennis was rebranded from the former ITTF moniker back in June, a move it said came with plans to raise investment and secure “new and stronger revenue streams” forming part of the governing body’s new strategic vision for the long-term sustainable growth of the sport.

Generali already has a strong presence in tennis, including title sponsorship of the Generali Open in Kitzbühel and a partnership with ATP player Dominic Thiem in Austria, sponsorship of the Monte Carlo Masters event, and partnerships with the Spanish and German tennis federations, alongside the aforementioned Davis Cup deal.

Visma | Lease a Bike counters Vollering's FDJ with an exclusive women's team sponsorship deal
article_text:
Rabobank is, of course, a well-known name in cycling, although its departure in 2012—due to the troubling doping scandals in the cycling peloton—wasn’t exactly on good terms.

After it also parted ways with the women’s team in 2016, the Dutch bank was absent from the cycling scene for several years. That is, until 2025, when it suddenly began sponsoring teams again.

In July of that year, it returned to Visma | Lease a Bike, initially as a partner of the men’s, women’s, and development teams.

It is also affiliated with the Dutch cycling federation and TeamNL, and organises events such as the Rabo NXT Classic, Ready2Race, and the Rabobank Dikke Banden Races.

Now, it is adding title sponsorship of the Visma | Lease a Bike women’s team to its portfolio.

For the women’s team, Rabobank is, of course, primarily filling a void that opened up after Visma scaled back its role within the organisation, transitioning from title sponsor to founding partner.

However, it also sends an important signal to women’s sports, where an increasing number of major sponsors are committing exclusively to women’s teams, without considering the men’s division.

Demi Vollering’s French team will be renamed TotalEnergies-FDJ United in 2027 and already has a major sponsor on board in Red Bull. As a result, Stephen Delcourt’s team has grown rapidly.

Visma | Lease a Bike has provided more details through official channels about its deal with Rabobank for 2027. The team will be called the 'Rabobank | Lease a Bike Women’s Pro Cycling Team' and represents “the next step in the partnership that began in 2025.”

"The title sponsorship underscores Rabobank's confidence in the team and its ambition to further grow women's cycling. Together, Rabobank and the team are developing initiatives to raise awareness of women’s cycling and encourage more girls to get on their bikes,” the team said.

CEO Richard Plugge calls it “a special moment” and is pleased with the trust placed by the bank. Carlo van Kemenade of Rabobank adds: “Our return sparked a lot of positivity and enthusiasm. By taking on a greater role in women’s cycling, we’re building on that. That aligns with our identity as a cooperative bank and our local commitment to the community.”

title: Bodø/Glimt lead global football clubs with 555 per cent social media growth in 2026
article_text:
Bodø/Glimt recorded the highest percentage increase in social media followers among the world’s leading football clubs in 2026, with their combined Instagram and TikTok audience increasing by 555 per cent between 1st January and 17th November, according to data platform Football Benchmark.

The club’s following grew from approximately 136,000 to 888,000, placing them at the top of Football Benchmark’s ranking of the ten fastest-growing clubs by percentage. Their 555 per cent growth rate was more than 2.7 times that of Chicago Fire FC, the second-ranked club, which recorded an increase of 205 per cent, with Turkish side Trabzonspor registering 140 per cent growth closing in the first three clubs with the biggest digital increase. Also worth highlighting is the contrast with Como 1907, the emerging force in Italian football, which ranked fourth with 138 per cent growth – more than five times lower than Bodø/Glimt’s figure. The analysis took into account only clubs with at least 100k total followers across Instagram and TikTok.

Having competed in Norway’s second division as recently as 2017, Bodø/Glimt have transformed their sporting standing through sustained development and consistent performances on the European stage. Last season’s Uefa Champions League campaign, featuring victories over Manchester City and Atlético de Madrid before eliminating Inter, further elevated the club’s international profile.

The figures demonstrate how sporting performance and European competition exposure can accelerate international audience growth, creating opportunities to strengthen brand positioning, expand commercial reach and attract new partners.

Bodø/Glimt’s achievement also highlights the changing dynamics of football’s global attention economy, where ambitious clubs can build significant international audiences through sporting credibility and a distinctive competitive identity, challenging the traditional dominance of established football brands.

Source: Football Benchmark Social Media Analytics Platform. Combined Instagram and TikTok followers, 1 January–17 November 2026.

Hull FC have signed sports performance brand Nutrition X as their nutrition partner, with players already using its products during the first weeks of pre-season training.

Founded in 2011, Nutrition X supplies performance and recovery products to professional sports clubs and athletes across the UK and Europe. Its sports nutrition range is built around education, science and safety. The brand will work closely with the Black & Whites’ performance and nutrition teams to support players through the 2027 season.

George Gladding, Club Partnership Executive at Nutrition X, said, “We are delighted to be building a partnership with Hull FC, bringing together two organisations that share a commitment to performance, development and success. We’re looking forward to working closely with the club’s performance and nutrition teams, providing the support, expertise and products to help players perform at their best.“

“We see this as the beginning of a long-term relationship and are excited to grow together, supporting Hull FC both on and off the pitch for many seasons to come.”

Grand Départ GB 2027 has appointed LS Events as delivery partner for the first team time trial in the history of the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift. The stage will close next summer’s British Grand Départ in London on Sunday 1 August 2027.

Seven-rider teams will race an 18km circuit through central London, starting on Whitehall and finishing on The Mall, where men’s Tour de France stages have finished twice before. Between 21 and 22 teams will compete, setting off at four-minute intervals.

LS Events will bring its experience of pan-London operations to a stage expected to draw hundreds of thousands of spectators along a route passing the Houses of Parliament, the London Eye and Tower Bridge. Across its three days, the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift is expected to be the most attended women’s sporting event ever staged in Britain.

Paul Bush OBE, Managing Director, Grand Départ GB, said: “The London stage of next year’s Grands Départs is going to be the finale to an amazing month of world-class sport in communities across Scotland, England and Wales, and LS Events’ experience of delivering major events in London make them the logical choice for Grand Départ GB to partner with. London is already a cycling city, so what better platform to showcase the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift with this amazing team time trial stage that will inspire the next generation of women cyclists.”

Jen-e Jones, Vice President of Operations, LS Events, said: “We’re delighted to be working with Grand Départ GB and the GLA to lead delivery of the stage three London team time trial. It’s one of the most complex sport operations we’ve delivered in the capital, and we’re proud to be the trusted partner for such a landmark event. On one day, the world’s best women riders will race past some of London’s most recognisable landmarks. It’s a pivotal moment for women’s cycling.“

Jones continues to add, “We’re responsible for the extensive logistics and preparation required for the route and operational leadership across the boroughs. That means traffic and crowd management, safety, spectator welfare, working with businesses and communities to ensure everyone benefits from the event, and dressing the city, all powered by Grand Départ JOY Maker volunteers, stewards and the LS Events core team. This will mark the very first Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift event in our capital city, and LS Events could not be prouder to bring our extensive ‘London’ experience to this ground-breaking event.”

In 2027 Britain will become the first nation outside France to host both the men’s and women’s race starts in the same year. The men’s race begins in Edinburgh on Friday 2 July 2027, and the women’s race starts in Leeds on Friday 30 July 2027, with stages from Leeds to Manchester and Manchester to Sheffield before the London finale. The events are supported by funding partners the UK Government, Scottish Government, Welsh Government, UK Sport and British Cycling.

The London stage is estimated to generate £12 million in economic impact for the capital, and marks the Tour de France’s return to London for the first time in 12 years. Organisers are targeting more than 10 million spectators across the six stages, with around 9,000 volunteer JOY Makers involved.

Founded in 2004 and led by Co-CEOs Steve Reynolds and Dave Grindle, LS Events has a portfolio that includes UEFA Champions League Final fan activations, Formula E, Emirates Great Britain SailGP, Soccer Aid, Operation London Bridge, Pride in London and American Express presents BST Hyde Park.

title: MLB launches preventative suit against MLBPA as lockout looms
article_text:
The elite Major League Baseball (MLB) has filed a class action lawsuit against the MLB Players Association (MLBPA), a preventative move it says is aimed at preventing an antitrust suit being leveled against it by the labor union.

Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) negotiations have shown no sign of bearing fruit, making the prospect of a lockout in 2027, and thus no baseball, likely.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Now, MLB claims that it has “a reasonable and imminent fear” that the MLBPA intends to use antitrust litigation as a tactic against the league.

MLB is the only major US league with a unique antitrust exemption, granted by the US Supreme Court in 1922, that shields it from federal commerce rules by legislating MLB games as local commerce rather than interstate commerce.

There is, however, a flaw, introduced in 1998 by the Curt Flood Act, which would allow MLB players to sue the league on antitrust grounds individually should the MLBPA be disbanded, as the 1922 exemption does not cover major league players.

The league believes the MLBPA could bring litigation against the league as an alternative to continued negotiations as a means of forcing through what it wants, which is a CBA without a salary cap.

It would do this by decertifying itself, something the league claims would be a ‘sham’ thus allowing the players to sue, claiming a lockout is illegal, and thus exposing MLB to heavy antitrust damages.

In a release, the league said that the suit is a measure “simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season.”

In a rival statement, the MLBPA called the lawsuit ‘frivolous’, saying: “We will respond appropriately, but MLB’s decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing.”

With this suit, MLB is seeking to establish firstly that a lockout is fully legal due to its exemption from antitrust law, secondly that even if it is not exempt, it would remain legal as it is now “an unreasonable restraint on trade,” and thirdly that federal courts do not have the jurisdiction to affect the lockout.

MLB is the only one of the four US major sports leagues to not enforce a salary cap, nor does it enforce a spending floor, which in recent years means that a large gap has developed between high-spending teams like the champion LA Dodgers (which has a payroll of around $420 million), and the low spenders like the Miami Marlins (payroll c.$78 million).

Effectively, MLB’s proposal outlines that owners will find it hard to achieve strong market value outcomes for selling their teams without a cap, as new investors would be loathe to spend lavish seven- or eight-figure sums on teams without parity guarantees.

The league claims that without a salary cap, it may find it hard to maintain a competitive balance among franchises, a factor that is harming franchise values, particularly at smaller-market teams.

That claim has taken a hit this season, as the World Series was won by the Milwaukee Brewers franchise, one of the smallest payroll teams in MLB, which swept past the Dodgers in the process.

Indeed, the MLBPA has often rejected narratives surrounding the salary cap as a positive measure, arguing that any cap would only serve to enrich owners, many of whom may not have to spend as much as before to compete, at the expense of players.

In its latest statement, the MLBPA said that MLB owners “continue to propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values.

The fact, then, that the World Series featured two small markets makes it perhaps the most timely edition in years, and one for which the aftershocks will reverberate for a while, despite the fairly elementary conclusion: a 4-1 Brewers win.

In the latest edition of the Sportcal Industry Insights podcast, GlobalData Sport lead analyst Conrad Wiacek and senior data researcher Will Padmore comb through those aftershocks, using data to benchmark the viewership statistics and dissect the league’s sponsorship and media rights strategy, as well as discussing what will come next in the CBA standoff.

This data is included in the GlobalData Sport Post Event Analysis – MLB World Series 2026, available on the GlobalData Sport Intelligence Center, which highlights the major themes surrounding the 2026 World Series, from the commercial partners to the strong attendance numbers (at record prices), and the media value presented by broadcaster Fox.

title: Rabobank becomes new title partner of…
article_text:
From the 2027 season, Rabobank will become the first title partner of Team Visma | Lease a Bike’s women’s team. Led by Marianne Vos and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, the team will continue as Rabobank | Lease a Bike Women’s Pro Cycling Team. This marks the next step in the partnership that began in 2025. Rabobank takes over from Visma, which will remain involved with the team as a Founding Partner.

The expanded partnership marks the prominent return of the Rabobank name to professional cycling, a sport in which the bank has a long history. Team leaders Marianne Vos and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, who both spent five years riding for the former Rabobank women’s team, will once again wear a Rabobank jersey from 2027.

The title sponsorship underlines Rabobank’s confidence in the team and its ambition to further grow women’s cycling. Together, Rabobank and the team will develop initiatives to raise the profile of women’s cycling and encourage more girls to take up the sport.

Rabobank and the team share the ambition to strengthen cycling at every level: from introducing children to the sport through initiatives such as the Rabo Dikke Banden Races to developing cycling talent and supporting riders competing at WorldTour level. Rabobank will also remain a Premium Partner of the men’s and development teams, retaining its existing logo positions on their jerseys.

This next step comes at a time when women’s cycling is experiencing significant growth, both in sporting terms and in terms of public and commercial interest. With Dutch and international talent, the women’s team offers Rabobank a powerful platform to contribute to this continued development. The team’s international profile also aligns well with the bank’s ambitions in key European growth markets.

CEO Richard Plugge is proud of this next step in the partnership with Rabobank: “Given our shared history, the return of the Rabobank name as a title partner is a special moment. It demonstrates Rabobank’s confidence in our team and in the future of women’s cycling. We are proud to build on that confidence together.”

Carlo van Kemenade, member of Rabobank’s Managing Board: “When we returned to cycling last year, our ambition was to give the sport a boost, with a focus on elite sport, talent development and grassroots sport in the Netherlands. Our return generated a great deal of positivity and enthusiasm. By taking on a greater role in women’s cycling, we are building on that momentum. This reflects who we are as a cooperative bank and our commitment to local communities. From the first introduction to the sport to competing at the highest level, we want to contribute to a sport in which talent has even more opportunities to flourish. For us, that is the power of investing in sport together.”

title: Leicester City FC bring in BettaBet as betting partner
article_text:
Leicester City FC have signed UK-based betting platform BettaBet as their exclusive UK betting partner until the end of the 2026/27 season.

Foxes supporters will get access to favourable odds, club merchandise and exclusive experiences through the deal. BettaBet will also appear across Leicester’s digital platforms and on Filbert Way on matchdays at King Power Stadium.

Russell Jones, Leicester City Commercial Director, said: “We’re pleased to welcome BettaBet to our partner network and look forward to building a successful relationship with them. The partnership will provide a platform for BettaBet to connect with our supporters through our digital channels and matchday activity at King Power Stadium.”

Daniel Shannon, VP of Marketing at Betable Group, said: “We’re incredibly excited to be partnering with Leicester City, a club with fantastic history, a passionate fanbase and strong reputation both in the UK and internationally. For us at Betable, this partnership represents another important step in our growth as we continue to strengthen our presence in the UK market.

“We’re looking forward to working closely with the club, bringing fresh ideas to the partnership and building a successful relationship.”

The agreement comes during Leicester’s first season in the third tier since 2008/09. The Foxes were relegated from the Championship in April, a decade after their 2016 Premier League title.

Betable provides the technology behind a number of sportsbooks licensed by the UK Gambling Commission. In the first half of 2026 it brought three brands to the UK market: Ivy Bet, RightBet and Bet442.

title: Visma dials back Visma | Lease a Bike sponsorship, remains founding partner
article_text:
Team Visma | Lease a Bike (VLAB), the leading road cycling organization, has confirmed that lead sponsor Visma will no longer serve as the team’s title partner going forward, although it will not completely divest from the team.

Visma has extended its partnership and will remain as a ‘founding partner’ of the team, but has opted not to continue with naming rights, an outcome that has been rumored for months.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The Norwegian tech brand has been a title sponsor of the team since 2019, and took over the lead sponsorship in 2024.

Visma is now the second such founding partner on the team’s roster after previous lead sponsor Jumbo, the supermarket chain, which stepped back from its role like Visma at the end of 2023.

Now Visma will dial back its commitment, although it will remain the team's official technology partner, and several Visma-owned tech brands will now appear on the VLAB jersey through the 2027 campaign.

Speaking on the announcement, VLAB chief executive Richard Plugge said: “It’s fantastic that Visma is extending its partnership with our team. Visma believed in our ambitions when we started working together in 2019.

“I’m grateful to everyone at Visma for the trust they’ve placed in us over the years. Having Visma stay with the team as a founding partner reflects what we’ve built together.”

The departure of Visma leaves a big sponsorship gap that needs to be filled, should the team wish to mount a strong 2027 campaign and avoid losing ground to rivals like Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, Lidl-Trek, and Decathlon AG2R La Mondiale, which have all bolstered their portfolios in recent years.

Sponsorship such as this is vital for cycling teams at all levels of the sport, the majority of which are almost entirely sponsor-funded.

If VLAB wishes to remain competitive against major rival UAE Team Emirates – XRG, and, crucially, retain top star Jonas Vingegaard in the long term, then further backing is needed.

The 2026 season was a mixed year for VLAB, with Vingegaard securing the Giro d’Italia Grand Tour general classification easily, but failing to challenge rival Tadej Pogačar in the Tour de France, before dropping out of that race due to injury and ending his season early.

Vingegaard’s position as arguably one of the top-2 riders in the sport will certainly be a key driver of VLAB’s sponsorship sales process. Earlier this week, the team expanded its partnership with major US sportswear brand Nike.

The Dane claimed back-to-back Tour de France wins in 2022 and 2023, as well as a Vuelta a España win in 2025, and the aforementioned Giro win this year, making him only the eighth rider in history to win all three Grand Tours.

Belgian icon Wout van Aert, young Brit Matthew Brennan, and 2023 Vuelta champion Sepp Kuss will also likely have factored into Nike’s plans, as continued broadcast presence at key points in races like the Tour de France is an important driver of sponsorship in cycling.

Before the 2026 Tour de France, VLAB chief business officer Jasper Saeijs suggested that cycling sponsorship fees represent a strong value proposition relative to the media exposure that WorldTour races, particularly the three Grand Tours, bring, saying: “We (VLAB) are one of the best sponsorship opportunities in sports.”

By comparison, Jonathan Vaughters, manager of the EF Education–EasyPost team, argued perhaps the opposite.

Remarking on the state of the sport and the effects of this period of dominance by a few privileged teams, Vaughters said: “The top teams are no longer a valuable proposition from a sponsor standpoint. A company could get its logo on a ninth-ranked Formula 1 [motor racing] team’s car for €20 million ($23.1 million), or they could invest it in a cycling team.

“But €20 million isn’t going to win them the Tour de France. There’s zero chance. Cycling used to be a valuable proposition, but we’ve lost that now.”

Cycling’s heavy reliance on sponsorship revenue, and that spending’s direct correlation with rider contract spending, has created a catch-22 situation where winning races requires top riders, access to top riders requires significant sponsorship revenue, and sponsorship revenue can only be grown by winning races.

This has effectively stratified the WorldTour peloton, with the top six-to-eight teams, backed by high-profile sponsors, billionaire investment, or sovereign wealth financing, performing at a level that the other sides, which rely on less lucrative sponsorship deals and, in many cases, face an annual struggle just to continue operations, cannot.

This dynamic was dissected earlier this year on the Sportcal Podcast, where GlobalData Sport lead analyst Conrad Wiacek and head of data Gordon Berry discussed VLAB's predicament and the varying perspectives on cycling sponsorship, where money in cycling comes from, and how teams can improve sponsorship values by maximizing their resources.

title: Sesame becomes the new Main Sponsor of Levante UD
article_text:
The leading comprehensive platform in talent and human resources management supports the club for the entire season.

Levante UD and Sesame, the leading comprehensive platform for talent and human resources management, have reached a sponsorship agreement through which the Valencian technology company becomes the Main Sponsor of the club starting from the 2026/27 season.

As the main sponsor of the men's first team, Sesame will feature on the front of the official game jersey as we already saw a few days ago with the launch of the first and second kits, on training gear, and on other physical and digital assets of the club. The agreement also includes a comprehensive program of activations, VIP experiences, corporate events, and content initiatives that will bring the brand closer to fans and the business community.

For Sesame, this sponsorship represents a key step in its brand positioning and visibility, associating itself with one of the historic clubs of Spanish football and a benchmark in Valencian sports. Additionally, this agreement reflects a growing trend in which high-growth technology companies seek to connect their brands with spaces capable of generating community, belonging, and shared emotions. For the company, football represents an environment where values such as teamwork, perseverance, and talent development are experienced every day.

“This alliance with Levante UD makes perfect sense for us. Football and scale-ups like Sesame have much more in common than it seems. Both of us thrive on building teams, developing talent, making quick decisions, and competing every day to improve. At Sesame, we believe that this way of understanding growth deserves to go beyond offices and connect with millions of people,” stated Albert Soriano, CEO of Sesame.

The head of Sesame also emphasized the local nature of the collaboration. “We are especially excited that this agreement is with a club from our homeland. We are a tech company born in Valencia that now works with companies all over the world, and we are very proud of our origins as well as being able to support Levante UD,” added Soriano.

For Levante UD, it is a great satisfaction to be associated with and display on their chest the brand of a Valencian technology company that is a leader in the field of human resources. “The arrival of Sesame as the main sponsor reinforces our commitment to innovation, professionalism, and continuing to grow hand in hand with companies that are transforming their sectors from Valencia to the world,” stated Pablo Sánchez, president of Levante UD.

Following the announcement of this agreement, Sesame and Levante UD are opening a new phase of collaboration in which various joint actions are planned, as well as the promotion of projects that go beyond sports sponsorship, bringing innovation, technology, sports, and the values of talent closer to Levante fans and society as a whole.

Sesame is human resources software focused on redefining the employee experience. It allows the digitalization of the most routine human resources processes so that managers and HR professionals can focus on talent, professional development, and the well-being of their teams, thereby growing their business and building a successful corporate culture. Currently, they have more than 20,000 clients in over 30 countries across Europe and Latin America.

kwiff confirms 2026 WDF World Darts Championship sponsorship
article_text:
The darts championship runs until early December.

kwiff, the super-charged sports betting service, is returning to Lakeside as a sponsor of the 2026 WDF World Darts Championship.

Kicking off today and running until December 6, the tournament is expected to welcome between 15,000 and 20,000 spectators, with kwiff delivering a comprehensive sponsorship activation spanning venue branding, fan engagement, broadcast exposure and digital content.

The popular kwiff Zone will return to Lakeside, giving fans aged 25 and over the opportunity to showcase their skills in a daily 9 Dart Challenge, with prizes supplied by Target Darts. kwiff’s branding will also feature on the iconic 180 signs held aloft by fans throughout the tournament.

Away from Lakeside, kwiff has secured live-streaming and social media clipping rights, enabling the brand to share tournament action and highlights across its digital channels. Additional brand exposure is planned across the WDF’s YouTube content.

To complement the sponsorship, kwiff has also joined forces with its existing football partners, Millwall FC and Blackburn Rovers FC, to produce a series of darts-themed videos. Players from both clubs have taken part in the kwiff 9 Darts Challenge and kwiff Bullseye Challenge, with content set to be released throughout the tournament.

Darts continues to resonate strongly with kwiff’s customers, ranking as the third most popular sport on the platform behind football and horse racing.

“Lakeside holds a special place in the world of darts, and we cannot wait to return for another edition of the WDF World Darts Championship,” said Jack Milner, sponsorship and partnerships manager at kwiff.

“Darts is a sport that really resonates with our customers, and this year we’re bringing together our on-site activation, digital content and existing football partnerships to extend the reach of our sponsorship well beyond the venue. Bring on a fantastic ten days of darts!”

This content has been published as part of a premium editorial package.

Fast cars, big money: Why sportswear races into Formula 1 as sponsorship spending soars 75%
article_text:
The race for dominance in Formula 1 is no longer confined to the racetrack, with some of the world's biggest sportswear brands, including Nike, Adidas and Puma, vying for a piece of the action.

Sportswear sponsorship spending in F1 has surged 75% over two years and topped $200 million in 2026, according to Adam Lewis, a senior analyst at research firm Ampere Analysis.

Brands are competing for access to the sport's increasingly young and affluent fan base, while looking to capitalize on its growing influence in fashion and popular culture.

Nike gave fans a sneak preview of its F1 partnership in Las Vegas this month with a limited-edition collection sold during the Grand Prix. From 2027, Nike will supply F1 staff uniforms, a role Puma has held since 2024, and sell footwear and apparel under the championship's brand.

Other sportswear majors have taken a different approach. Adidas signed with Mercedes in 2025 and added Audi for its debut season this year, while Puma still has its longstanding deal with Ferrari, covering racewear and licensing for Ferrari-branded products.

Unlike football leagues such as the English Premier League, where sportswear brands spread their budgets across numerous clubs, F1 has just 11 teams, limiting the number of apparel partnerships up for grabs.

"F1, by contrast, is a closed market with only a handful of teams," Lewis said, adding that the scarcity of deals makes brands more willing to pay higher prices as contracts come up for renewal.

What makes F1 particularly attractive, however, is its growing influence.

"For major sportswear and lifestyle brands, F1 has grown beyond motorsport, into a powerful, year-round pop-culture and storytelling platform," Joey Khong, global consumer trends manager at market research firm Mintel, told CNBC.

F1 brings together fashion, music, luxury and celebrity culture with athletic performance and technological innovation, offering brands multiple avenues to engage with consumers, Khong said.

Team apparel has also crossed over into everyday streetwear, with social media amplifying the visibility of what drivers and team members wear off the track.

Some 34% of people who engage with F1 do so through social media, while 22% engage through online content, according to Lewis.

That constant stream of content has turned team apparel into what Lewis described as a "living billboard" for sportswear brands.

Nearly a third of F1 fans are now under the age of 35, with that share rising 18% since 2023, according to Lewis. Meanwhile, 45% of F1 fans fall into the two highest-earning socioeconomic groups, compared with 36% of the general population.

For sportswear brands, F1 offers a way to build loyalty among younger, affluent consumers.

Asia-Pacific has been a key driver of F1's fan growth, helping deliver a larger audience for its commercial partners, analysts said.

Markets across the region have gained more than 25 million F1 fans since 2023, up 36%, according to Ampere Analysis. That outpaced growth in other markets by 11 percentage points and accounted for 84% of overall fan growth.

That offers sportswear brands a growing audience to engage with in a region where F1 already races in Melbourne, Suzuka, Shanghai and Singapore.

Research also points to why that engagement could resonate. In a 2026 Mintel survey, 29% of respondents in China said sporting events would prompt them to pay attention to or try related brands, rising to 37% in households earning at least 24,000 yuan ($3,600) a month.

Fans are spending more on F1 merchandise than ever before.

F1 merchandise sales have grown by almost 200% since 2017, according to Fanatics, the sport's e-commerce partner, cited in a License Global report.

Retail sales of F1-licensed consumer products also rose 44% in 2024, one of the fastest growth rates among the sports properties tracked.

The appeal may stretch beyond race-branded gear. F1 fans were 29% more likely than the average consumer to say they planned to buy sports apparel in the next year and 27% more likely to say the same about non-sports apparel, according to Ampere's consumer research.

Mintel's Khong said F1 merchandise alone is unlikely to move the needle quickly for sports apparel giants the size of Nike or Adidas.

Instead, the bigger potential payoff could come from the partnership boosting demand across the brand's everyday product lines outside F1-specific collaborations or the sport's licensed merchandise.

"There is a route to revenue growth, but being associated with the sport is only the starting point," Khong said.

title: Equiti Group Named Official Fintech Partner of 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s
article_text:
Equiti Group has secured the role of Official Fintech Partner for the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s, deepening its presence in the UAE’s sports and entertainment sector. For fintech professionals, the move highlights a growing trend of regional brokerages leveraging high-traffic cultural events to bridge the gap between complex financial services and mass-market consumer engagement.

The partnership positions Equiti Group as a primary sponsor for the 2026 edition of the Emirates Dubai 7s, scheduled to take place at The Sevens Stadium from 27 to 29 November 2026. The event serves as the opening for the 2026/27 HSBC SVNS season and features 28 international men’s and women’s rugby sevens teams competing across the HSBC SVNS and HSBC SVNS 3 tiers. Following a 2025 event that attracted over 88,000 attendees, the 2026 festival will include rugby, padel, fitness competitions, and the festival's first Gaelic football tournament.

Equiti’s involvement includes pitchside branding and digital screen visibility throughout the venue. In the Festival Village, the fintech will host a co-branded pop-up basketball court in collaboration with Dubai Basketball, offering free play to attendees. The company is also promoting its "Yalla Club," a free fan community designed to drive engagement through basketball shoot-out competitions and prize giveaways, including jerseys signed by Dubai Basketball players. This strategy aims to mirror the fast-paced nature of rugby sevens—a format characterized by two seven-minute halves—with accessible financial technology and habit-building tools.

"We are proud to partner with the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s, a pinnacle event on the UAE sporting calendar that brings elite international sport and community passion together under one roof. At Equiti, we believe in backing sport at every level and showing up where fans connect, making this iconic festival a natural fit for our values."

Equiti Group is a global fintech firm headquartered in Dubai that has evolved from a regional brokerage into a multi-asset financial services provider. Recently named a UAE Superbrand for 2025, the group operates across several international markets, providing technology-driven market access. The firm has established a significant footprint in the Middle Eastern sports ecosystem; it is a Founding Partner of Dubai Basketball, a front-of-shirt sponsor for Al Wahda FC, and the title sponsor of Dubai’s Youth Football League.

The Emirates Dubai 7s is the Middle East’s largest sports and entertainment festival. It is a cornerstone of the global rugby sevens circuit, a high-speed variant of rugby union that gained significant international visibility following its Olympic debut in 2016. The festival combines elite professional competition with grassroots sports, attracting a diverse demographic of international tourists and local residents. By partnering with a fintech entity, the festival continues to diversify its commercial portfolio beyond traditional beverage and travel sponsors, reflecting the UAE's status as a global hub for financial innovation.

FF News has closely followed Equiti Group’s aggressive expansion and technical integration strategy. In late 2026, the firm moved to partner with Botim to streamline trading account funding for UAE users. This followed a significant technical upgrade where the group integrated TradingView to enhance its multi-asset CFD offering. Beyond software, Equiti has focused on infrastructure and brand visibility, launching an AI-powered technology hub in India and expanding its front-of-shirt sponsorship with Al Wahda FC for the 2026/27 season.

This partnership signals a shift in how fintech firms approach customer acquisition in the Middle East. Rather than relying solely on digital performance marketing, firms like Equiti are moving into "lifestyle fintech," embedding their brands into high-energy physical events to build trust and community. This puts pressure on traditional retail banks and older brokerages that have historically been slow to engage with younger, sports-focused demographics. The challenge for the sector remains whether these high-visibility sponsorships can convert festival-goers into long-term active traders, or if the "fan community" approach serves primarily as a brand awareness exercise in an increasingly crowded UAE financial market.

Equiti Group has become the Official Fintech Partner of the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s. The partnership brings together a global fintech headquartered in Dubai and the Middle East's largest sports and entertainment festival around a shared belief: world-class experiences should bring more people into the action.

Rugby sevens is the fast-paced, seven-a-side format of rugby union that made its Olympic debut at Rio 2016. Teams play two seven-minute halves on a full-size pitch, with more space to attack than in the 15-a-side game. A single turnover can take a team from defending its own try line to racing towards the other end in seconds.

Emirates Dubai 7s brings world-class rugby to Dubai while giving grassroots teams a place alongside the international sides. Equiti brings that same mindset to finance, using technology to broaden market access without compromising quality and helping people build stronger financial habits.

Under the agreement, Equiti will feature pitchside and on screens across the venue. In the Festival Village, Equiti and Dubai Basketball will bring their co-branded pop-up court, where friends and families can play for free between matches. Fans can join Yalla Club, Equiti's free fan community, to enter a basketball shoot-out for a chance to win prizes from the Equiti tuk tuk. Equiti will also give away jerseys signed by Dubai Basketball players.

"We are proud to partner with the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s, a pinnacle event on the UAE sporting calendar that brings elite international sport and community passion together under one roof. At Equiti, we believe in backing sport at every level and showing up where fans connect, making this iconic festival a natural fit for our values." - Chantelle Johnson, Equiti CMO.

title: Softball Australia Signs WorldHotels as Official Partner in Three-Year Agreement
article_text:
Softball Australia has signed global hospitality network WorldHotels as an Official Partner under a three-year commercial agreement spanning high-performance national pathways and major international event delivery.

The partnership places the WorldHotels logo across the playing helmets of the Australian women’s national softball team, the Aussie Spirit, throughout the three-year term, including at the upcoming World Baseball Softball Confederation (WBSC) Women’s Softball World Cup Finals 2027 in Redcliffe, Queensland.

Operating a portfolio of 18 brands and more than 4,000 hotels across over 100 countries, WorldHotels joins an expanding commercial roster for the national governing body alongside inaugural Finals sponsor A.G. Coombs, apparel partner S-Trend, and training supplier PTP.

Commenting on the partnership, Softball Australia chief executive officer, Sarah Loh, said: “I’m delighted to welcome WorldHotels to the Softball Australia family.”

“To have a globally-reconised brand on board as an Official Partner for the next three years, including the WBSC Women’s Softball World Cup Finals, is exciting for the growth of softball in Australia and a strong endorsement of where our sport is heading.

“As we build to hosting the world’s best softball nations in Redcliffe, Queensland, in April 2027, partnerships like this play a crucial role in supporting our high-performance programs, delivering a world-class event and leaving a lasting legacy for softball in Australia,” Loh said.

WorldHotels Australasia managing director, Rod Munro, highlighted the alignment between the group’s international hotel footprint and Australian softball’s build-up toward Los Angeles 2028.

“Softball Australia is entering an exciting new era, and we are proud to be part of that journey.”

“We look forward to supporting athletes, staff and stakeholders across Australia, and helping to create a memorable experience at the WBSC Women’s Softball World Cup Finals 2027.

“The World Cup will leave a significant legacy for the sport and provides an important launchpad on the road to the LA28 Olympic Games and beyond.

“It is a privilege to support Softball Australia both nationally and international throughout this journey.

“With 18 brands, more than 4,000 hotels across over 100 countries, this partnership is a natural fit as we work together to support the growth and success of Australian softball,” Munro said.

Commercially, the multi-year term provides Softball Australia with international accommodation capacity and brand backing across a critical Olympic qualification cycle.

Staged at Kayo Stadium in Redcliffe from 5 to 11 April 2027, the eight-team WBSC Women’s Softball World Cup Finals will award a direct berth to the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games, where softball returns to the Olympic programme, creating high-value broadcast exposure and international visitor demand across south-east Queensland.
