title: DOJ probing NFL over potential antitrust violations in TV deals, sources say - ABC News
article_text:
It's said to involve whether customers are forced to pay more for subscriptions.

The Justice Department has opened an inquiry into whether the National Football League violated anticompetitive practices in its TV deals and then required customers to pay too much in subscription costs, according to three sources familiar with the probe.

The Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 gives some limited protections for the NFL which allows for sports leagues to pool broadcast rights.

"This is about affordability and creating an even playing field for providers," a government official told ABC News.

The Justice Department declined to comment. The Wall Street Journal first reported news of the probe.

In a statement to ABC News, the NFL defended its distribution model.

"The NFL's media distribution model is the most fan and broadcaster-friendly in the entire sports and entertainment industry," it said. "With over 87% of our games on free, broadcast television, including 100% of games in the markets of the competing teams, the NFL has for decades put our fans front and center in how we distribute our content. The 2025 season was our most viewed since 1989 and reflects the strength of the NFL distribution model and its wide availability to all fans."

Sen. Mike Lee, a Utah Republican who has been publicly urging the Justice Department to investigate the NFL's conduct, cheered news of the antitrust probe on his X account.

"Instead of a small number of free broadcast networks, the NFL now licenses games simultaneously to subscription streaming platforms, premium cable networks, and technology companies operating under different business models," he said on X.

"To the extent collectively licensed game packages are placed behind subscription paywalls, these arrangements may no longer align with the statutory concept of sponsored telecasting or the consumer-access rationale underlying the antitrust exemption," he posted.

"That's why, as chair of the Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights, I urged the DOJ to examine the Sports Broadcasting Act and its applicability to current media landscape. I'm glad they're tackling this," he said.

title: Foot Locker in as presenting partner of NBA Manchester game
article_text:
Basketball’s elite NBA has announced that shoe retailer Foot Locker will serve as the presenting partner of its upcoming international game in the UK.

Foot Locker will activate around the event with ‘fan engagement experiences’ across Manchester and at the 23,500-capacity Co-op Live venue.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The game, which will take place at Manchester’s Co-op Live arena on January 17, 2027, will see the New Orleans Pelicans take on the San Antonio Spurs as the second of two fixtures between the pair in Europe, the other taking place at France’s Accor Arena.

For Manchester, this will mark the city’s second-ever NBA game (it hosted a pre-season fixture in 2013) and its first-ever regular-season fixture.

Foot Locker has sponsored the league for well over a decade in a variety of markets, including Europe, the US, and Australia.

Around the game, the NBA has also partnered with credit card giant American Express to bring its NBA House activation to Manchester, following similar activations in London, UK, and Berlin, Germany, alongside the 2026 NBA international games in those cities.

In terms of broadcast coverage, likely a key driver behind the sponsorship agreement, the game will be broadcast by Amazon-owned OTT platform Prime Video.

Prime Video’s 11-year broadcast partnership with the NBA, struck in advance of the 2025-26 season, is worth $1.8 billion per year, and covers an expanded package of games in select territories, including Mexico, Brazil, France, Italy, Spain, Germany, the UK, and Ireland.

This expanded package includes a minimum of 20 additional primetime regular-season games each year, a Conference Finals series each year, and the NBA Finals in six of the 11 years.

Since that deal began, Prime Video has reported 184% viewership growth year-on-year for its NBA coverage in Europe, with the UK (+312%) and Germany (+246%) markets performing particularly well.

title: GB, French, German swimming bodies launch annual competition
article_text:
The governing bodies for swimming in Great Britain, France, and Germany have teamed up to launch a new annual international competition as they seek to modernise the sport and attract new audiences.

The 3 Nations Cup is a joint venture between Aquatics GB, the French Swimming Federation, and the German Swimming Federation and will debut in Manchester on March 14, 2027, before moving to Paris on March 21.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The new annual series will feature 22 races over 90 minutes. Mixed relays sit alongside women’s and men’s 50m ‘skins’ races in butterfly, backstroke, and breaststroke. Six swimmers will start, with four advancing, and just two reaching the final round.

To add an element of engagement and interaction to the team contest, spectators will draw the swimming order for the mixed 4x200m freestyle relay.

Points will count across both legs, and the team at the top of the standings after Paris will take the 3 Nations Cup title and share the prize money.

Through the 3 Nations Cup, the three federations said they are “creating a fresh way for fans to experience elite swimming, and a new platform through which to engage audiences, broadcasters, and commercial partners.”

Drew Barrand, Aquatics GB CEO, said: “It is time for elite swimming competition to evolve. Together with our counterparts in France and Germany, we have created a series that puts the excitement of racing at its heart.

“We want fans to feel the pressure of every race. With elimination rounds, mixed relays and points carrying across two weekends, the 3 Nations Cup gives them a fast-paced team contest to get behind from the first start to the final touch.

“This is a shared venture and a shared ambition. Leading from the front means putting new ideas into action, and all three nations are bringing that commitment to the pool.”

Next month, the International Swimming League (ISL), the club-based professional series, will also be making its return.

The league's upcoming one-night relaunch event, the ISL All-Star Match, will take place at the London Aquatics Centre in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park on December 19.

The All-Star Match will see the world's fastest swimmers compete in a team-based, two-hour, head-to-head competition.

Stakeholders in the sport are increasingly looking to maintain annual interest in swimming outside the Olympics through frequent, short-form competitions.

For British swimming, the 3 Nations Cup opens a three-part season in 2027, ahead of the Aquatics GB Swimming Championships in London in April and the World Aquatics Championships in Budapest in July.

Live coverage is planned for both legs of the 3 Nations Cup, with broadcast details to follow.

Earlier this year, the European Broadcasting Union (EBU), the continent’s association of public-service broadcasters, expanded its partnership with Aquatics GB to boost the visibility of international events in the UK.

The expanded agreement will see an increase in the range of events available free-to-air (FTA) in the UK throughout the year, including swimming, diving, artistic swimming, and open water swimming, via the Eurovision Sport streaming service, which will be embedded within the Aquatics GB website.

title: Sports Direct Signs Major Five-Year Deal with Shamrock Rovers
article_text:
Shamrock Rovers have confirmed a major new commercial partnership with Sports Direct Ireland, which will become the club’s official front-of-shirt sponsor from the 2027 season.

The five-year agreement covers both the men’s and women’s senior teams and is one of the biggest commercial partnerships in the history of the Tallaght-based club.

The partnership goes well beyond the standard shirt sponsorship model, with the two organisations committing to a range of fan engagement initiatives, community activities and exclusive supporter experiences.

There will also be a significant retail element to the relationship with the new Shamrock Rovers kit going on sale via nine Sports Direct stores across Dublin and Kildare, giving the club a much broader high street presence.

The financial terms of the agreement have not been disclosed.

“We’re absolutely delighted to be welcoming Sports Direct as our new Front of Shirt partner’ said CEO Robbie Hedderman.

“This is one of the most significant commercial deals in the history of the club, and it reflects the ambition we have for Shamrock Rovers both on and off the pitch.”

“Sports Direct is a brand that shares our belief in the power of sport to bring people together, and it is very important to us that their name will be on the front of the shirt worn by both our Men’s and Women’s senior teams.”

“Beyond the shirt, we’re very excited to be working with Sports Direct on a number of new initiatives to support our fans and to extend the reach of our Community Foundation from Tallaght and beyond.”

The deal sees another property added to Sports Direct’s significant investment in Irish sport, as part of its wider programme of sponsorship across Gaelic games and football.

“As one of the most iconic and successful clubs in Irish football, we’re very excited to be embarking on this new chapter with Shamrock Rovers,” said Leonard Brassel, Managing Director at Sports Direct Ireland.

“Together we want to create opportunities for the fans, support the wider community and help inspire more people to get involved in sport.”

The new 2027 kit will be available in Sports Direct stores at The Square Tallaght, Henry Street, Liffey Valley, Blanchardstown, Carrickmines, Finglas, Maynooth, Naas and Newbridge.

It’ll also be available from the club store at Tallaght Stadium in December, of course, capitalising on the key Christmas retail period.

A five-year commitment from a major international retailer is another clear vote of confidence in the League of Ireland’s commercial direction and gives Shamrock Rovers a degree of financial certainty to build on.

The fact that both senior teams are in is a good thing, and the commitment to the Shamrock Rovers Community Foundation’s work is obviously a positive.

The retail side is the most interesting. Getting League of Ireland merchandise into mainstream sports goods stores alongside the merchandise of big international clubs would be a massive boost to the game’s profile and would expose the club to a whole new audience.

Competition between brands for a foothold in Irish football is obviously increasing, and this deal is another clear sign of the commercialisation of the domestic game.

Sports Direct and Shamrock Rovers are full members of the Sport for Business Community. If you would like to join them and see your organisation in our content, on our stages, and in the daily conversation around the commercial world of Irish Sport, email us today and let’s see what is possible.

Sport for Business is Ireland’s leading platform focused on the commercial, strategic and societal impact of sport. It connects decision-makers across governing bodies, clubs, brands, agencies, and public institutions through high-quality content, events, and insights.

Sport for Business explores how sport drives economic value, participation, inclusion and national identity, and how your story can be part of ours.

Through analysis, storytelling and convening the sector, it helps leaders understand trends, share best practices, and make better-informed decisions. It positions sport not just as entertainment but as a vital contributor to Ireland’s social and economic fabric.

Or sign up for our Daily Sport for Business Snapshot email bulletins to get a flavour of the material we cover.

title: Futsal Malta Association and Bank of Valletta sign naming rights agreement
article_text:
The Futsal Malta Association has announced a new partnership with Bank of Valletta, which will see BOV acquire the naming rights of the Futsal Trophy for both the men’s and women’s competitions for the next three seasons.

The agreement was signed by Ernest Agius, Chief Operations Officer, and Manya Vittoria Pisani, Corporate Social Responsibility Manager, on behalf of Bank of Valletta, together with Futsal Malta Association president Nathaniel Jones, vice-president Kurt Bonnici, general secretary Andy Mangion and treasurer Clayton Scicluna.

FMA president Nathaniel Jones expressed his satisfaction that a prestigious institution of national significance such as Bank of Valletta has chosen to partner with the association and lend its support to the sport.

Jones emphasised that this partnership is a testament to the growing importance of futsal in Malta, as well as the sport’s considerable potential and promising future.

The agreement represents another important milestone in the development of local futsal, further strengthening both the men’s and women’s competitions.

title: SportVot gives Liga Portugal trio coverage in India, Sri Lanka, Maldives
article_text:
Portuguese soccer’s top-tier Liga Portugal has increased its international visibility by securing SportVot, the live sports streaming platform, as a new broadcast partner in India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives.

The new agreement sees SportVot secure exclusive streaming rights to league matches involving Liga Portugal’s three most renowned clubs – Sporting CP, Benfica, and FC Porto – which it will air on its platform.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The deal was brokered by international sports marketing agency Sportfive, which serves as the league’s international media rights partner through 2027-28. The deal covers global markets outside Portugal ahead of Liga Portugal’s transition to a centralized rights model starting in 2028-29.

Shubhangi Gupta, co-founder of SportVot, said, "Football has a passionate and growing audience across India and South Asia, and we're excited to bring matches featuring clubs like Sporting CP, Benfica and FC Porto to fans in these markets.

“Acquiring these rights is an important step in building SportVot's international content portfolio and making more quality live sporting action accessible to audiences through our platform."

The deal marks the first time Indian audiences will have access to Liga Portugal matches through a dedicated streaming platform and opens the league up to a potentially lucrative new market.

The deal is the latest move by SportVot to pivot beyond domestic and emerging sports and into premium sports content, having earlier this year secured exclusive streaming rights in India for 2026 summer club friendlies, covering pre-season matches across the Premier League, LaLiga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, and Liga Portugal.

Meanwhile, the new agreement comes as Liga Portugal looks to boost its international visibility, having yesterday announced a rights deal in Australia with nascent digital soccer platform Football360 for the remainder of the 2026-27 season.

Under its agreement, Football360 will stream two matches per week via its website, as well as replays on demand, mini matches, highlights, and short-form video content across its website and social media channels.

Earlier this year, international OTT sports streaming service DAZN acquired rights to show three Liga Portugal matches per game week for the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons exclusively in Japan, Italy, and Belgium and non-exclusively in Spain.

Shortly after, German sports channel Sportdigital extended its exclusive broadcast rights to Liga Portugal through the 2027-28 season.

title: Saran renews LaLiga rights in Türkiye through 2031-32
article_text:
Saran Media Group, the prominent Turkish media operation, has renewed its rights for Spanish soccer’s top-tier LaLiga for another five years.

The renewed agreement, which runs from the 2027-28 season through 2031- 32, will see Saran Media Group continue to provide coverage of league matches via its S Sport television channel and S Sport Plus streaming platform across Türkiye.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The renewal builds on the pair’s original broadcast agreement, which began with the 2022-23 season, and has seen Saran Media Group provide expert commentary and analysis alongside live matches.

Turkish players including Arda Güler (Real Madrid), Enes Ünal (Getafe) currently play in LaLiga, with the league having previously featured leading players such as Nihat Kahveci, Arda Turan, Altay Bayındır, Çağlar Söyüncü, and Okay Yokuşlu.

LaLiga president Javier Tebas said: “Türkiye is a strategic market for LALIGA, with a young, highly engaged and digitally connected football audience with a growing bond with our clubs and players.

“Our international strategy puts fans at the center, making it easier for them to follow their favourite players, clubs and rivalries, with an experience that feels local and goes beyond the 90 minutes.

“Long-term partnerships with broadcasters that combine local knowledge, distribution strength and the ability to tell the story of the competition are fundamental to that ambition.”

The renewal consolidates Saran Media Group’s burgeoning soccer rights portfolio, headlined by a recently secured deal to show the 2027 Women’s World Cup national team tournament in 24 European and Eurasian countries and rights to UEFA national team tournaments for the 2024 to 2028 cycle.

The media group also holds exclusive rights to English soccer’s Premier League and knockout FA Cup competitions across a range of Eastern European and Central Asian territories through 2027-28 and German soccer’s top-tier Bundesliga in a four-year deal running through the 2028-29 campaign.

Its rights for Italian soccer’s top-tier Serie A involve Saran holding rights in Turkey and Ukraine between 2024-25 and 2026-27, and in another 13 markets (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan) from 2024-25 through 2028-29.

Saran also has a five-year media rights management deal in place with French soccer's LFP body. Through the deal, Saran exclusively manages the media rights of the top-tier Ligue 1, second-tier Ligue 2, and the Coupe de France, in 18 Central Asian and Eastern European markets through 2028-29.

Other soccer rights include the Dutch Eredivisie and the Saudi Pro League, while other sports properties covered include basketball’s Euroleague and NBA, ATP Masters 1000 tennis tournaments, motorcycling’s MotoGP, American football’s NFL, and the Volleyball Nations League.

Kenan Saran, Chairman of Saran Media Group, said: “We are extremely proud to extend a partnership that has been going strong since 2022 and delighted to continue bringing LaLiga to Turkish football fans for another five seasons.

“Following our recent rights extensions across eight European markets, alongside our existing presence in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan, this agreement further reflects our growing regional reach, our broadcasting capabilities and our long-term commitment to delivering the world's best sports content.”

title: Team Marketing enters motorsport with Pramac Racing remit
article_text:
Pramac Racing, the prominent motorcycle racing organization, has hired prominent sports and commercial agency Team Marketing to lead the development of its sponsorship portfolio.

The team, which competes in the elite MotoGP series as Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP, and in the secondary Moto2 category as BLU CRU Pramac Yamaha Moto2 Team, is aiming to add more “international brands” to its partnership roster, ahead of a prospective entry into the Moto3 category.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

A focus of this agreement, Pramac says, will be the aim of bringing in sponsor brands from outside the traditional motorsport industry.

This represents Team’s first deal in the motorsport sector, as the organization widens its reach beyond its initial European soccer remit.

Speaking on the announcement, Pramac Racing chair Paolo Campinoti said: “We are proud to announce our partnership with Team and welcome them to motorsport. We‘re confident they will achieve the same breakthrough results they‘ve delivered in football and across the broader sports industry, and we‘ll be part of this important growth.

“Team understands the international sponsorship market and has demonstrated its expertise in reaching new brands across multiple sectors. We're looking forward to working together to develop those opportunities.”

Team chief executive Simon Crouch added: “Pramac Racing has built an impressive track record under Paolo Campinoti's leadership, and we see significant opportunities to introduce new brands to the sport and help Pramac Racing build on its success. MotoGP is entering an exciting period, and we‘re honoured to contribute our commercial expertise beyond football.”

Pramac is likely aiming to capitalize on its recent success, having in 2023 become the first independent (non-factory) MotoGP team to win the Team World Championship, followed by a 2024 campaign that saw rider Jorge Martin (now of Aprilia Racing) win the Riders World Championship.

A key component of that plan will be to capitalize on the presence of Turkish rider Toprak Razgatlıoğlu, a three-time Superbike World Champion, who entered the MotoGP circuit ahead of the 2026 season.

Although his debut campaign was marred by poor team performance and injury, the presence of a successful driver from an area that is not a traditional MotoGP market in Turkiye may lead to strong commercial possibilities for Pramac.

For Team Marketing, meanwhile, the new business win comes as it faces a future without its biggest client, European soccer’s UEFA governing body, after three decades of marketing the global media and commercial rights for its men’s club competitions, including the top-tier Champions League.

Its contract with UEFA, which excludes US media rights, ends after the 2026-27 season, with Relevent taking over the global marketing mandate from 2027-28.

In February 2025, the agency announced its commercial partnership with UEFA had generated over €50 billion in cumulative revenue for European club soccer.

This week, the agency has also added English rugby union club Wasps as a client, with the goal of supporting its return to professional status.

The long-term partnership, running until June 2031, will see Team serve as Wasps’ full-service marketing agency, working to develop its commercial strategy, strengthen its brand and secure long-term partnerships.

title: Rivers United secure N490m shirt sponsorship deal
article_text:
Rivers United Football Club of Port Harcourt has secured a three-year front-of-shirt sponsorship deal worth $350,000 (about ₦490m) with Goka Sports and Casino.

The partnership was officially unveiled in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on Wednesday.

Speaking at the event, the Sole Administrator of Rivers United, Christopher Green, said the club rejected Goka’s initial proposal for a one-year contract in favour of a longer-term agreement.

Green said, “Goka wanted a one-year contract with an extension, but we said no. We’ll go for three years first, with an upward renewal.

“So the deal is worth three hundred and fifty thousand US dollars, which is four hundred and ninety million naira in Nigerian currency.”

He expressed optimism that the agreement would attract more commercial partners, revealing plans to secure additional sponsorships for other areas of the team’s playing kit.

“With this, we’ve opened the door for more sponsorship deals. In no time, we will get the one for the back shirt, one for the sleeve and the others.

“It marks the biggest front-of-shirt sponsorship agreement in the history of the Pride of Rivers and one of the most significant commercial deals in Nigerian football,” Green added.

He further disclosed that discussions were underway to extend Goka’s involvement to Rivers Hoopers, the state’s basketball team.

According to him, “We have been talking to Goka and we have also sold Rivers Hoopers to them. Soon they will come for the same front-shirt sponsorship.”

Speaking on behalf of Goka Sports and Casino, the company’s representative, Jide Odi, described the agreement as a privilege, acknowledging that reaching the unveiling stage had not been an easy process.

He said the company had carefully assessed Nigerian clubs, considering their history, coefficients and standing in domestic football before deciding to partner with Rivers United.

“We’re here to stay, we’re not going anywhere. Goka is here to expand the frontiers of private partnership with sports in Nigeria, and we’re starting with Rivers United,” Odi said.

He explained that the club’s ambitions aligned with Goka’s vision of expanding private-sector investment in Nigerian sports.

Odi also highlighted the importance of football as both a community-driven activity and a business, expressing hope that the agreement would create more opportunities for both parties.

He regretted that the sponsorship unveiling did not take place before Rivers United’s 6-0 victory over Niger Tornadoes, saying it would have been exciting to see the new Goka branding on the team’s shirt during the emphatic win.

However, he reiterated the company’s commitment to a long-term relationship with the club, expressing hope that the agreement would open the door to more partnerships capable of advancing Nigerian football.

“This is just the first step in the long-term relationship. We’re looking to expand the conversation in partnerships and to see how we can take Nigerian football forward,” he added.

Meanwhile, Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, commended Green for his efforts in managing the club, particularly for securing the partnership with Goka Sports and Casino.

The governor, who was represented at the event by a former Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Communications, Mike Elechi, said Goka’s investment in the club would require returns through the sale of branded jerseys.

He also commended the company for choosing Rivers United for the partnership.

title: What Fifa’s US$2bn 2030 World Cup rights auction will reveal about soccer in the US
article_text:
Fifa’s auction of the 2030 and 2034 Fifa World Cup rights in the US will reveal much about soccer’s position in a sporting ecosystem that has for so long dismissed the sport as a foreign pursuit best served by niche outlets.

The greatest result in the national team’s history, a 1-0 victory over England at the 1950 World Cup, warranted barely a mention in the contemporary local press. Even a host of superstars led by Pele and rule changes designed to attract US audiences couldn’t make the North American Soccer Legue (NASL) a success.

But in the four decades since the NASL shuttered in 1984, a four-decade project to make the world’s game America’s game has borne fruit. It’s a journey that began by awarding the US the 1994 men’s World Cup and has seen triumphs in the women’s edition, the launch of professional leagues for both, and the arrival of Lionel Messi in Major League Soccer (MLS).

The foundations laid by USA 94 allowed the 2026 tournament in North America to become a major national event. Average viewership was up by 116 per cent from Qatar 2022 to 7.7 million across Fox’s flagship network, its FS1 cable channel, and its Tubi streaming platform, with matches also carried on the broadcaster’s Fox One streaming service.

The final itself attracted 65 million viewers on Fox and the Spanish language Telemundo, making it the most-watched live sporting event other than the Super Bowl since Nancy Kerrigan and Tonya Harding appeared in the figure skating event at the 1994 Winter Olympic Games.

The US is no longer an afterthought for Fifa and its thinly-veiled desire for further revenue growth – it is now arguably its most important market.

Early antipathy for soccer was reflected in World Cup broadcast arrangements. NBC’s delayed transmission of the 1966 final was the first standalone soccer broadcast in US history, but coverage was either absent or limited to highlights until 1982 when ESPN and cable television arrived.

It wasn’t until 1998 that every game was shown live. Even now, the Spanish language rights command a higher premium than those in English.

Fifa now has an attractive product in the world’s largest and most lucrative sports media market where consumers are willing to pay.

Not only that, but it’s also free from pesky regulators who insist on free-to-air (FTA) coverage and limit the number of commercials that can be shown during an hour of broadcast television in most countries in Europe, limiting the number of potential bidders and the amount Fifa can earn.

World soccer’s governing body exercised this freedom during the summer by allowing broadcasters to air advertising during three-minute hydration breaks during each half. Ostensibly, this was a measure designed to aid player welfare during high temperatures. However, the breaks were mandatory regardless of temperature.

This predictable break allowed Fox to charge premium rates to advertisers during the actual game itself – allowing it to further monetise its assets.

Fifa predictably attempted to distance itself from accusations of overcommercialisation by (rightly) claiming that it made no additional revenue from the measure as the broadcast contracts had been finalised long before its decision.

But there is no denying that the 2026 World Cup – and Fox’s revenues – will increase the value of future deals, especially in a country like the US where fans are regularly bombarded with advertising during National Football League (NFL) games.

The World Cup has proven itself as a ratings winner at a time when traditional broadcasters and steamers are desperate for live sporting rights. These are the only guarantee of huge live audiences in the modern media landscape and are an effective subscriber acquisition and retention tool.

Changing consumption habits coupled with rising interest in soccer have seen the Premier League, Uefa Champions League and several other European competitions secure lucrative deals with streaming services, eager to fill their platforms with content and attract a highly engaged, relatively diverse audience that is willing to pay to watch their favourite sport.

With 104 matches at a time when only Major League Baseball (MLB), the Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA) and a few other leagues have their regular seasons, the World Cup has the volume and schedule that potential media partners value.

And, on top of that, it can harness the power of patriotism and its status as the most prestigious prize in the sport to generate the crossover appeal witnessed in the summer.

Accordingly, virtually every single broadcaster and streamer in the US has been linked with a bid for the rights – raising the prospect of a bidding war between some of the most well-resourced broadcasters in the world and big tech companies with pockets deeper than the Mariana Trench.

In the event, only two bidders registered their interest before last week’s deadline – Fox and Netflix. While the bean counters in Zurich might be disappointed, there is virtually no scenario beyond an inexplicable act of God that would prevent Fifa from enjoying a significant uplift in media rights revenue.

Back in 2011, Fox paid US$425 million for all men’s and women’s tournaments between 2015 and 2022, while Telemundo forked out US$600 million. At the end of that contract, you might have expected Fifa to cash in on seven years of soccer growth Stateside and the prospect of a home World Cup in 2026 delivering unprecedented interest and huge ratings.

Indeed, many observers believed that the rights could have been worth up to US$1.5 billion for 2026 alone. There was just one problem. Instead of putting the rights out to tender on the open market, Fox had been handed the rights for US$485 million back in 2015 – years before the hosting rights had been awarded to North America.

title: WTW becomes Everton insurance partner
article_text:
Global advisory and broking firm WTW has joined Everton as insurance partner in a multi-year deal, extending its growing footprint in English football.

As Everton’s exclusive partner in the insurance brokerage category, WTW will provide the club with tailored risk and insurance advice and solutions. The deal also gives it brand visibility at Hill Dickinson Stadium and across Everton’s digital and social channels, alongside commercial activation rights and access to the stadium for client hospitality and business events. The partners may also develop community initiatives over the course of the deal.

Since opening in August 2025, the 52,769-capacity stadium has hosted the Rugby League Ashes and an England Women’s international. It is also a host venue for Euro 2028, and Everton have applied to double the number of non-sporting events, including concerts, held there each year.

The Everton agreement follows WTW’s deal with WSL Football in September, under which it is working to co-create an insurance product for players across the Barclays Women’s Super League and Women’s Super League 2. WTW is also global insurance partner of the INEOS Grenadiers cycling team and places more than $100m of sports premium in global insurance markets each year.

Ian Tomlin, Global Sports and Entertainment Leader at WTW, said, “High-performing organisations, whether in sport or business, depend on resilience, specialist expertise and the confidence to make informed decisions. Our partnership with Everton brings together the Club’s ambition and distinctive identity with WTW’s global insurance, risk and analytics expertise. Together, we will help create greater resilience, improved risk management and performance, and lasting value on and off the pitch.”

The deal is Everton’s second commercial agreement in three days, following the arrival of US power technology brand NOCO as battery charging partner.

Mark Rollings, Chief Partnerships Officer at Everton, said, “WTW is a highly respected global business with an outstanding reputation for expertise and innovation. This is a relationship that brings together two organisations with shared ambitions and a commitment to long-term success. Welcoming another business of WTW’s calibre is a further demonstration of our commercial

title: Shorts: Sky, Newcastle Red Bulls, PWR
article_text:
Sky has brought together leaders from sport, broadcasting, business and politics to launch the Game Changing Coalition. Its aim is to close the gap between girls’ and boys’ participation in sport.

Chaired by former Sports Minister Dame Tracey Crouch, the coalition held its first meeting this week. Founding members include Sky Sports CEO Jonathan Licht, WSL Football CEO Nikki Doucet, the Premier League’s Chief Football Officer Rebecca Caplehorn, the ECB’s Chief Revenue Officer Aarti Dabas and Judy Murray. They are joined by Baroness Sue Campbell, Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson, Anita Asante and Ebony-Jewel Rainford-Brent, alongside senior figures from The FA, World Rugby, UEFA, Nike, YouTube, Deloitte, Barclays, Howden Group and Mumsnet.

According to Sky’s Game Changing report, girls spend 1.4 fewer hours a week playing sport than boys, the equivalent of missing 52 football matches a year. Coalition members reach more than 750 million people through their platforms and together invest millions each year in sport, physical activity and grassroots programmes.

The coalition will work across three pillars, Play, Watch and Attend, and will set clear, accountable goals. Constituency-level research will help it target the communities with the lowest participation. With the UK set to host the 2031 Netball World Cup and the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup, the group also aims to help build a lasting legacy from both tournaments. Sky will revisit its research at the end of 2028 to measure progress.

Dame Tracey Crouch, Chair of the Game Changing Coalition, said, “Despite many excellent initiatives, progress in women’s sport remains stubbornly static. What makes this coalition different is the unique mix of voices lending their influence, expertise and resources to the cause that can help drive meaningful change. By harnessing that collective power with commercial backing, we can break down barriers at scale and ensure every girl, regardless of her background or where she lives, has the opportunity to get active and stay active.”

Jonathan Licht, CEO of Sky Sports, said, “Too many girls are experiencing barriers to playing sport, and the result is 280 million missing hours of sport a year compared to boys. Closing that gap isn’t just about getting more girls active, it’s about giving them the opportunity to build confidence, make connections and develop skills that will benefit them throughout their lives. That is why we are using Sky’s unique position in the UK to bring together sporting and commercial organisations with the influence to drive lasting change.”

Sky is also supporting The Equal Sport Project, which launched on 10th November with the ambition of making the UK the world’s leading nation for women and girls’ sport.

Newcastle Red Bulls have signed Destination Sport as their travel supplier in a multi-year deal, starting with a chance for supporters to fly with the team to Lyon in the EPCR Challenge Cup.

Destination Sport is a global travel business built for sport, with a portfolio of specialist brands connecting teams, rights holders, events, fans and participants. The partnership brings together its elite team travel and fan experience expertise, with plans to expand into youth development tours.

The first trip, organised through Destination Sport’s fan travel brand SportsBreaks, takes supporters to Newcastle’s Challenge Cup match against LOU Rugby at Matmut Stadium on Sunday 17th January 2027. Packages include return flights on the team charter from Newcastle, one night’s accommodation, airport and stadium transfers and staff support. Bookings close on Thursday 3rd December.

The deal adds to a run of partnerships at Kingston Park, following the recent arrival of Thatchers as cider partner and Ad Gefrin as whisky supplier.

Jonny Petrie, Managing Director of Newcastle Red Bulls, said, “We’re delighted to welcome Destination Sport as our Official Travel Supplier. They have a wealth of experience in professional team travel and fan experiences, and we look forward to working with them to build on this expertise to develop our supporter travel offering.“

“Our trip to Lyon in January is a great way to get things started, giving our supporters the opportunity to travel with the team, get behind the lads in Europe and make their presence felt away from home.”

Steve Butchart, Managing Director of Elite & Youth at Destination Sport, said, “We are delighted to announce this new multi-year agreement with Newcastle Red Bulls. This is a partnership that really demonstrates the breadth of Destination Sport’s offering, bringing together specialist expertise in elite team travel and fan experiences, with a view to expanding into youth development tours under one joined-up solution.

“Newcastle Red Bulls is a club with a proud heritage and exciting ambition for the future, and we’re excited to bring our specialist travel services to the club to help support that ambition over the coming years.”

English sparkling wine producer Nyetimber has become sponsor of the Player of the Match award in Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR), extending its partnership portfolio in English rugby.

Across all 21 rounds of the 2026/27 JAECOO PWR season, each Player of the Match will receive a magnum of Nyetimber Classic Cuvee Multi-Vintage.

Nyetimber was the first to plant the classic sparkling wine grape varieties in the UK, in 1988. Its Head Winemaker, Cherie Spriggs, became the first woman and the first person from outside Champagne to be named Sparkling Winemaker of the Year at the International Wine Challenge in 2018. She won the award again in 2025 and remains the only woman to have done so.

The PWR deal builds on Nyetimber’s wider support for the sport. The brand became England Rugby’s sparkling wine partner in 2025 and is served at all England home matches at Allianz Stadium. It also sponsors Richmond Rugby and has signed England captain Jamie George as a brand ambassador.

CONCACAF expands regional sponsorship with Mexico’s Caliente.mx
article_text:
North American soccer’s CONCACAF has renewed and expanded its partnership with Mexican betting company Caliente.mx to cover the governing body's major men’s and women’s national team competitions.

The new agreement will see Caliente.mx continue as an official sponsor in Mexico, covering the 2027 and 2029 editions of the Gold Cup, the men’s flagship national teams competition, with the partnership also expanding to include the upcoming women’s 2026 W Championship national team tournament, as well as the 2027 and 2029 editions of the men’s CONCACAF Nations League Finals.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The expansion builds on the pair’s previous agreement, which started with last year’s CONCACAF Gold Cup and expanded earlier this year to include the next two editions of the men’s and women’s top-tier Champions Cup club competitions.

Heidi Pellerano, CONCACAF chief commercial officer, said: “We are delighted to continue growing our partnership with Caliente.mx, a partner that shares our ambition to bring fans closer to the game.

“This expanded agreement reflects the strength and appeal of our competitions and creates new opportunities to engage passionate football audiences across men's and women's football.”

The expansion comes days before the 2026 W Championship, which will be held across two stadiums in Texas from November 27 to December 5. Texas Health Mansfield Stadium is set to host the quarterfinals, semifinals, and play-in matches, while Shell Energy Stadium will host the third-place match and the final.

The tournament, featuring eight teams, acts as a qualification competition for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 and the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

Fernanda Sainz, chief commercial officer of Caliente.mx, added: “Renewing our partnership with Concacaf reaffirms our long-term commitment to national team football and allows us to continue supporting the region’s major sporting moments.

“The addition of the Concacaf W Championship also provides an opportunity to raise the profile of women’s football, recognize the talent of its players and help more women make their mark both on and off the pitch.”

The announcement follows CONCACAF announcing significant format changes to the Gold Cup from the 2027 edition.

Instead of the 16 competing teams at next year's Gold Cup being split into four groups, each comprising a quartet of sides, there will instead be two groups of eight teams each.

The 2027 Gold Cup will involve 15 teams from the region, as well as Saudi Arabia, who have been invited by the CONCACAF soccer governing body.

A host for the tournament – set to take place between June 17 and July 11 – has still not been selected.

CONCACAF's aim through splitting the teams into just two groups, instead of four, is to bring about more games at the event between the top-ranked teams, as early as possible in the Gold Cup.

After the group stages, the top four sides in each group will qualify for the quarterfinals.

Eight of the teams present at the Gold Cup will be qualifying through the 2026-27 CONCACAF Nations League, taking place currently.

Late June saw US media giant Fox renew its English-language rights deal covering the Gold Cup through 2029, with the agreement also covering the CONCACAF Nations League.

This came after TelevisaUnivision retained Spanish-language rights – also in the US – in May.

title: Nike expands Visma | Lease a Bike sponsorship with kit branding
article_text:
Team Visma | Lease a Bike (VLAB), the leading road cycling organization, has expanded its commercial partnership with sportswear giant Nike, which will now sponsor the team’s jerseys and will collaborate on technical innovation.

Although Nike will not actually serve as VLAB’s kit manufacturer, which remains Italian brand Nimbl, the two companies will work together to develop and innovate on kit design and technology.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Both Nike and Nimbl’s brands will feature on VLAB race suits going forward through the 2027 campaign, while Nike will also continue to provide off-bike apparel for riders and staff, as it has done since the 2025 Tour de France.

This is not the first collaboration between Nike, VLAB, and Nimbl, which has been the team’s kit supplier for several seasons already, as the pair made limited edition race suits and cycling shoes for the 2026 Giro d’Italia and Tour de France races respectively, while the pair also have a collaborative cycling equipment collection separate to the VLAB deal.

Speaking on the expanded deal, VLAB chief executive Richard Plugge said: “We set a high standard for everything that helps us win, and that includes our kit. Nimbl is a specialist that shares that ambition. Bringing Nike Cycling’s expertise and creativity into the partnership opens up new possibilities for us.

"Few brands have done as much as Nike to bring sport and athletes to a global audience. We’re proud to bring that experience into our partnership with Nike Cycling and take this next step together. We want to build something together that moves both our team and the sport forward.”

Nike has a history in cycling, most notably through its long-term endorsement of American rider Lance Armstrong, from 1998 through to the revelation of his significant doping malpractice in 2012, which saw Armstrong effectively blackballed from the sport, while Nike stepped back from the peloton.

In recent years, though, Nike has re-entered the road cycling category somewhat, through the off-bike apparel deal with VLAB and leading women’s cycling team FDJ-Suez (soon to be renamed FDJ-TotalEnergies), which may also now be a target for Nike to further expand its presence in the sport.

2026 was a mixed year for VLAB, with top star Jona Vingegaard securing the Giro d’Italia Grand Tour general classification easily, but failing to challenge rival Tadej Pogačar in the Tour de France, before dropping out of that race due to injury and ending his season early.

Vingegaard’s position as arguably one of the top-2 riders in the sport will certainly have been a key driver of Nike’s sponsorship.

The Dane claimed back-to-back Tour de France wins in 2022 and 2023, as well as a Vuelta a España win in 2025, and the aforementioned Giro win this year, making him only the eighth rider in history to win all three Grand Tours.

Belgian icon Wout van Aert, young Brit Matthew Brennan, and 2023 Vuelta champion Sepp Kuss will also likely have factored into Nike’s plans, as continued broadcast presence at key points in races like the Tour de France is an important driver of sponsorship in cycling.

Before the 2026 Tour de France, VLAB chief business officer Jasper Saeijs suggested that cycling sponsorship fees represent a strong value proposition relative to the media exposure that WorldTour races, particularly the three Grand Tours, bring, saying “We (VLAB) are one of the best sponsorship opportunities in sports.”

Sponsorship such as this is vital for cycling teams at all levels of the sport, the majority of which are almost entirely sponsor-funded.

Cycling’s heavy reliance on sponsorship revenue, and that spending’s direct correlation with rider contract spending, has created a catch-22 situation where winning races requires top riders, access to top riders requires significant sponsorship revenue, and sponsorship revenue can only be grown by winning races.

This has effectively stratified the WorldTour peloton, with the top six-to-eight teams, backed by high-profile sponsors, billionaire investment, or sovereign wealth financing, performing at a level that the other sides, which rely on less lucrative sponsorship deals and, in many cases, face an annual struggle just to continue operations, cannot.

This dynamic was dissected earlier this year on the Sportcal Podcast, wherein GlobalData Sport lead analyst Conrad Wiacek and head of data Gordon Berry discussed the varying perspectives on cycling sponsorship, where money in cycling comes from, and how teams can improve sponsorship values by maximizing their resources.

title: Sevens test an elementary decision for New Zealand ‘rookie’ Holmes
article_text:
Her name is familiar - and the jersey is, too - but otherwise it’s all change for Renee Holmes as the new HSBC SVNS Series begins.

A Women’s Rugby World Cup winner in 2022, and with 33 test caps to her name, Holmes has made the switch to sevens and will make her debut for the Black Ferns Sevens in Dubai this weekend.

The shift to the shorter form of the game marks a full-circle moment for Holmes, who moved from football to sevens in 2018 and won New Zealand Rugby’s talent-scouting Ignite Sevens competition in 2019.

Apart from a short period early last year, Holmes has been a Black Ferns mainstay since her debut in 2021 and is their second all-time leading test points scorer.

The move to sevens has nothing to do with her wanting away from 15s, but rather an unwillingness to be left with an Olympic-sized “what if?” on her personal CV as she returns to the format of the game where she first started.

“I’ve come over 18 months out from the Olympics where usually you’re with the team for the four-year cycle, so it’s definitely a big jump - but just in terms of where I am in my career, the timing of this all, I think it's probably perfect, and if I give it a good nudge, I will never have that regret, I’ll always remember at least I tried,” she said.

Looking to freshen up after the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, where the Black Ferns finished third, Holmes asked to train with the sevens team over the Christmas-New Year period and travelled with the development side to the Coral Coast tournament in January in Fiji.

It led to something entirely unexpected.

“I did not anticipate falling in love again with the game,” Holmes said. “I just saw the growth, how much I was learning in a short period of time and how exciting the game was.

“After the Super Rugby Aupiki season I reached out to [Black Ferns Sevens coach] Cory Sweeney again and asked if I could come in for a proper preseason, give myself that time to condition myself to the sevens game, and understand and learn what they do in that space - and, yeah, now I’m here, and getting into a full season of sevens.”

Holmes was a standout during the Super Rugby season having moved to the Hurricanes Poua, a team that had previously been the competition’s easy beats.

Having played the bulk of her career at full-back she slotted in at fly-half where her exceptional kicking game and calm head provided a catalyst for the Poua’s revival.

Although they ultimately fell short of making the final, Holmes says her season with the Wellington-based side coupled with the support of Poua coach Hayden Triggs and Black Ferns’ assistant Riki Flutey has given her the confidence to make the move to sevens.

“I genuinely feel uncomfortable every day, because I don’t know what it looks like, I don’t know what skill set we are using each day,” she admitted.

“Some of these girls have been doing a drill for the last eight years, but this is my first time. We had the Mount Sevens as a preseason hit-out a few weeks ago, so I got exposure to more countries – and, man, every game was different, we had a different game plan, each team played a different style, and it was all over in 14 minutes. It’s just so exciting and refreshing,” Holmes said.

Holmes has come into a Black Ferns Sevens side smarting from the end of the 2026 HSBC SVNS campaign where, having won six tournaments, they fell away in the last two events to lose the Valladolid and Bordeaux finals and ultimately the World Championship to Australia.

With Sarah Hirini, Michaela Brake and Shiray Kaka making their way back after giving birth, and Stacey Waaka absent after playing rugby league, there’s a fresh look to this season’s Black Ferns Sevens squad. Holmes hopes her experience can add a point of difference in Dubai and Cape Town.

“I’ve been playing fly-half, hooker, working prop, starting and coming off the bench in preseason, so that versatility and bringing a kicking ability as well, is something I want to maintain,” she said.

“Restarts and conversions have been areas that this team is working towards becoming world class and world-leading in that space, so that’s really exciting for me.”

Still only 26, Holmes’s extensive CV and handful of years as a professional means she understands what it takes to cut it at the highest level, although she concedes a full sevens pre-season has taken her, “to some dark places”.

She’s also relishing her time living back near the beach and tapping into the wisdom of her flatmates who know a thing or two about the game. She’s living with Portia and Renee Woodman-Wickliffe.

Holmes will wear number 35 this season, a reference to the state highway that connects her home region on the east coast of Aotearoa’s North Island. Holmes, sevens team-mate Kelsey Teneti, World Rugby Player of the Year Kaipo Olsen-Baker and Black Ferns test captain Ruahei Demant all hail from the area, which is rugged and somewhat remote, a place of natural beauty but where some people can do it tough.

“Lu [Demant] and I always say, ‘35 for the world’ when we go out to training because our community is so small, but there’s so much talent. To be able to pull on that jersey with that number and showcase a bit of what’s come out of home and so people from there can see what we can do will be very special.”

title: Newcastle Jets Re-Sign Alka Power as Official Hydration Partner for 2026/27 Season
article_text:
The Newcastle Jets have re-signed Australian alkaline beverage brand Alka Power as the Official Hydration Partner across both the club’s A-League Men’s and A-League Women’s teams for the 2026/27 season.

The renewed agreement restores category exclusivity for the functional beverage supplier across the Hunter region franchise’s senior football programmes.

Founded in 2012, Alka Power distributes its high-pH alkaline water nationally across major supermarkets, independent grocers, and petrol and convenience retailers, leveraging elite domestic football partnerships to reinforce everyday health and cellular hydration positioning among active consumers.

Alka Power managing director, Steve Pettaras, highlighted the value of returning as exclusive hydration partner across both senior Jets squads for the 2026/27 campaign.

“Alka Power is again proud to return as the exclusive Hydration Partner of the Newcastle Jets men’s and women’s football teams.

“As a natural high pH alkaline hydration water, we know how important it is that players keep hydrated on a cellular level.

“That’s why Alka Power has been the number one alkaline water brand for well over a decade. Best of luck to all for the 2026/27 season,” Pettaras said.

Dual-Squad Category Exclusivity: Secures exclusive Official Hydration Partner status covering both the Newcastle Jets A-League Men’s and A-League Women’s programmes throughout the 2026/27 season.

High-Performance Product Supply: Supplies naturally high-pH alkaline hydration water to support player recovery and hydration management across domestic A-League and continental AFC Champions League Elite schedules.

National Retail Leverage: Connects on-field club visibility with Alka Power’s nationwide distribution footprint across major supermarkets, independent grocery chains, and convenience outlets.

title: Erebus Motorsport Confirms Greenworks Naming Rights for Adelaide Grand Final and TotalEnergies Expansion into 2027
article_text:
Erebus Motorsport has announced two commercial partnership expansions ahead of the Adelaide Grand Final, with Greenworks Australia confirmed as the Primary Partner and Naming Rights Partner of Car #9 for the season-closing round, and TotalEnergies extending its commitment across both Cars #99 and #9 for the 2027 Repco Supercars Championship.

Greenworks Australia’s partnership with Erebus Motorsport began at the Taupō round of the New Zealand double-header in April 2026, when the brand’s branding first appeared on the front guard of Jobe Stewart’s Chevrolet Camaro. For the Adelaide Grand Final — the final round of the 2026 Supercars season, with track action commencing Thursday 26 November 2026 — that presence expanded considerably.

Greenworks branding is positioned to take pride of place across the bonnet and both doors of Car #9 for the Adelaide event. The company describes itself as a global leader in battery-powered tools, offering emissions-free solutions across home, commercial and professional applications.

TotalEnergies, whose Quartz Engine Oil brand will continue as a prominent feature on the TotalEnergies Quartz Chevrolet Camaro, will retain major naming rights on Car #99 while significantly increasing its branding presence on Car #9 for the 2027 season. Jarrod Hughes, newly confirmed as an Erebus Motorsport signing, will drive Car #99 in 2027.

Both announcements were made in the week of 25 November 2026, ahead of the Adelaide Grand Final. Erebus CEO Barry Ryan and COO Carly Hammersley have each characterised commercial partnerships as central to the independent team’s operations and long-term growth.

The Greenworks arrangement grew from a single-round placement in April 2026 to full naming rights inside eight months. TotalEnergies’ 2027 commitment spans two cars rather than one.

title: Tony Romo lands first sponsorship deal since drunk driving arrest
article_text:
Tony Romo’s got a new gig, but it’s not one that’ll put him back in the broadcast booth.

The former CBS analyst, ousted from his role with the network last month after he was arrested in July for allegedly driving under the influence, announced on Wednesday he’s joining forces with Jake Paul’s sports betting company, Betr.

Romo’s title, according to the former Cowboys quarterback, will be “Chief Predictions Officer.”

“I’m Back,” he wrote in announcing his next endeavor on Instagram. “New Job. Same Goal.”

Betr said in a press release that Romo’s role with the organization will include “appearing in original content, delivering sports predictions and engaging fans across the company’s expanding ecosystem of gaming products.”

The company, which touts itself as “the world’s first real-money gaming super app,” also stated Romo “will become an equity stakeholder” with his new job.

“I’ve spent my entire career trying to anticipate what’s going to happen next, whether that was on the field or in the broadcast booth,” Romo said. “Now I get to put those instincts to work in a completely new way with Betr.”

Paul, alongside Joey Levy, founded the business in 2022, and prior to Romo, it had some big celebrity endorsers, including former Heisman Trophy winner Johnny Manziel and ex-NBA player Patrick Beverley.

Romo had been looking for work since Oct. 2, when he and CBS parted ways following his July 23 run-in with cops in Wisconsin.

Police accused Romo of getting behind the wheel of his car while intoxicated, and after an eventful traffic stop, cops hit the four-time Pro Bowler with four citations, including one for OWI and one for possessing open intoxicants in a moving vehicle.

Romo pleaded no contest to OWI as part of a plea deal he struck in September with prosecutors to close out the case and he lost his driving privileges for six months as part of his sentencing.

Romo said after the ordeal that he had developed “an over-reliance on alcohol” due to injuries he sustained during his NFL career and he vowed to take some time away from the spotlight to work on his health.

title: Nike’s post-Lance return to cycling accelerates with Visma-Lease A Bike sponsorship
article_text:
There was a time when Nike was ubiquitous in cycling. As in most other sports, the global powerhouse had its instantly recognisable Swoosh stamped all over the peloton. Most prominently, all over Lance Armstrong.

When the Armstrong bubble went bust in 2012, the Swoosh all but disappeared. Now, 15 years later, Nike’s comeback is ramping up. Visma-Lease A Bike announced Nike will step up its involvement in the team, supporting Nimbl as the team’s supplier for the 2027 season, and joining Nimbl on the team’s jersey.

This isn’t Nike’s first step back into cycling though. While the brand was mostly absent from the sport, aside from a personal sponsorship of Mark Cavendish, it has slowly inched its way back into the peloton, or adjacent to it, over the last three years. The Visma-Lease A Bike deal accelerates a slow comeback to cycling for the U.S. brand. That started with the blockbuster signing of Demi Vollering back in 2024. That deal was for off-the-bike apparel, though it soon expanded to include Vollering’s FDJ-Suez (now TotalEnergies FDJ United) teammates.

The following year, Nike and Visma-Lease A Bike formed a similar partnership for off-the-bike apparel. Nimbl would supply the team’s race kit and shoes while Nike would clothe athletes off the bike.

So what’s today’s news, if Nike already sponsors the team? Now Nike and Nimbl will, for starters, both appear on the team’s jerseys. More notably, Nike Cycling will also be supporting product development going forward.

“Nimbl brings its expertise in materials, fit and customisation, while Nike Cycling supports development with its expertise in innovation and design,’ Visma-Lease A Bike’s announcement reads. “The expanded partnership brings together the team’s elite racing insight with sport science and athlete-performance expertise from across Nike. It gives Team Visma – Lease a Bike, Nimbl and Nike Cycling more opportunities to develop and test new ideas together under the conditions in which the riders compete. ”

Nike already made a couple appearances on the bike in 2026, as the announcement notes, with special edition shoes and kits for big races. It looks like that partnership was successful enough that it is expanding.

Nike isn’t the only big name getting back into the game, though. Its move from casual to performance gear mirrors the strategy of a long-time rival brand.

Adidas has made similar moves, supporting Mathieu van der Poel and his Alpecin-Premier Tech team with off-the bike apparel. The three stripes are taking a broader approach, though. Adidas is also the title sponsor of Norco adidas Race Division, the Canadian-based downhill World Cup team, as well as several individual freeride athletes. With both the team and individuals, the casual sponsorship paved the way for adidas’s return to performance gear. That move is slightly complicated off-road, as adidas owned footwear brand Five Ten. But at the Norco team, within a year the casual wear turned into a full launch of adidas-branded Freerider Pro race shoes for 2027, marking the stripes proper return to racing off-road.

As we’re seeing with Visma-Lease A Bike, Nike is following a similar playbook in the peloton. Casual, then performance.

And this could be just the start. Even Visma’s own announcement hinted that much more could be in the works, staking its claim to be “The first team to announce its Nike Cycling partnership for the 2027 season.”

That sure sounds like there’s more to come.

Will we see a return to the adidas and Jan Ullrich vs Nike and Lance era of brand rivalry on the road? If we do, it’ll be different in a few ways. First, both brand’s are supporting teams with prominent women’s programs, not just the boys club. Second, cycling is, hopefully, much cleaner than it was in that era. Even the most winningest cyclist of this new era says so.

title: New documents reveal SEC’s role in preventing mandatory media-rights pooling in PCSA
article_text:
Awful Announcing previously documented how ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro was lobbying New York Yankees President Randy Levine, a leader of the president’s college sports committee and advocate for the Protect College Sports Act, to protect the network’s television deal with the SEC. New documents show the goal was mutual from the SEC’s side.

Emails obtained via public records requests detail how one of the conference’s main objectives with the bill was keeping its lucrative media deal with ESPN and staying out of the PCSA’s proposed media pool. They show the SEC telling senators it wouldn’t support the PCSA unless media rights pooling was optional and telling its members to turn down meetings with the bill’s primary advocacy backer, Saving College Sports, because of the group’s support for the provision.

On Aug. 4, SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey emailed every SEC president and athletic director about a call scheduled for later that day. Organized by SCS with Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-MO), the call would address the next steps for the PCSA. The SEC had announced its support for the bill just days earlier.

The invitations cited conference support for the legislation and suggested conference leaders or school representatives would participate, Sankey wrote. Several SEC officials had contacted him to ask about the group and its invitation.

Sankey said he wouldn’t participate. He cited SCS’s support for “centralized media-rights negotiations for college football, greater national coordination of football scheduling in support of those media-rights objectives, and a national approach to distributing revenues generated through those media rights,” as reasons to oppose the bill. Those goals were “inconsistent with longstanding SEC principles and policy positions,” Sankey wrote.

He also instructed SEC officials to decline SCS invitations even when they came through significant donors, governing board chairs, or board members. Attendance, “even solely for informational purposes,” could later be characterized as support for the group’s objectives.

“Regardless of the source, I recommend that these invitations be respectfully declined,” Sankey wrote.

Saving College Sports declined comment for this story. As of publication, the SEC has not responded to Awful Announcing’s request for comment.

Records obtained from multiple SEC universities include a June 12 document listing the conference’s “red provisions” for the PCSA under the heading “Must be fixed.”

“There should be no question that joining the covered entity is voluntary and that declining to join has no legal ramifications,” the document stated. It called for an explicit prohibition on state or federal lawsuits challenging a decision to stay out of the pool. The SEC also wanted to prevent participating conferences or the pool itself from using new agreements or other actions to compromise nonparticipants’ rights or pressure them to join.

The document sought to exclude all postseason tournaments and contests from pooling. It warned that the bill could otherwise “interfere with existing tournaments, such as the College Baseball or Softball World Series.”

In a cover memo dated the same day, Sankey instructed presidents and athletic directors to call both of their senators before the committee markup. He supplied a script asking senators to support the conference and their school “by withholding your support for the Protect College Sports Act until essential revisions are made to strengthen the legislation.”

SEC talking points obtained from Texas stated: “We do not believe media rights pooling is necessary to stabilize college athletics.” The document argued that pooling legislation should be considered separately. The talking points said the SEC did not oppose other conferences and universities opting in. Its concern was that the proposal “exposes the SEC to potential lawsuits, forcing the conference into the media pooling practice.”

By July 26, Senate Commerce Committee staff members were offering changes to address those concerns. Sankey circulated a summary of proposed revisions that afternoon, along with an email from Brad Grantz, the committee’s majority staff director. Grantz described the attachment as a summary of changes “to secure [the SEC and Big Ten’s] support.”

“This is a substantial package, and much of it reflects what you have specifically asked us to change,” Grantz wrote. The attachment paired requests with proposed provisions. Under “Keep Media Rights Voluntary,” it said the act would not permit federal or state lawsuits challenging an institution’s or conference’s decision to stay out.

Another entry addressed scheduling. Earlier versions of the PCSA contained a traditional rivalry provision that would have required Oklahoma to put Oklahoma State back on its schedule and Missouri to do the same with Kansas. The Senate response said those requirements would apply only to institutions that voluntarily joined the pool. Schools and conferences that stayed out would be exempt, regardless of whether a game was a traditional rivalry.

Sankey wrote that the summary “reflects progress.” Grantz subsequently sent a “best-and-final offer,” copying Levine. The package included the voluntary participation and scheduling protections the SEC had sought.

“Pencils are down,” Grantz wrote. He demanded individual responses by 10 a.m. July 30 stating whether recipients supported the bill and would actively work to secure its passage.

On July 31, Sankey forwarded another message to SEC presidents saying the committee had “moved substantially in the SEC’s direction.” It cited voluntary participation, scheduling authority for nonparticipants, and protection from litigation intended to force them to join.

“There is no legislative alternative that gets better for the SEC,” the message warned. Further revisions protected existing television agreements, including ESPN’s SEC deal, from being overridden by a pool. The bill also expressly stated that conferences and institutions could not be required to join.

title: Italy see off Fiji fightback to end miserable run
article_text:
Italy ended their seven-match losing streak to edge Fiji 23-21 but the clash between the Nations Championship’s lowest ranked teams was watched by a sparse crowd at Allianz Stadium.

Billed as the ‘Super Bowl of rugby’, finals weekend has struggled to attract interest with only 32,000 general admission tickets sold for day one, resulting in Twickenham’s entire top tier being closed.

Acting as the curtain raiser to the fifth place play-off between Ireland and Australia later on Friday night, Fiji and Italy at least delivered a hard fought battle that went down to the wire.

Sumptuous second-half tries by Peniasi Dakuwaqa and Kitione Salawa propelled the Islanders into the lead, reeling in Italy who had established a 17-0 lead built on touch downs by Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera.

Ultimately it was the boot of Tommaso Allan that proved the difference with the former Harlequins full-back landing a decisive 68th minute penalty to complete a 13-point individual haul.

Fiji played some thrilling rugby in pursuit of a late victory but their execution was poor with a knock-on close to the line and wayward line-out throw important moments that cost them.

Italy defended well and showed greater discipline to end a losing run that dated back to their historic victory over England in the penultimate round of the Six Nations.

title: Rugby World Cup: Next four hosts confirmed as Spain bids
article_text:
European rugby fans could be spared a 16-year wait for the men's Rugby World Cup to return to the continent after Spain entered the race to host the 2035 tournament.

World Rugby has already confirmed the hosts of its next four men's and women's tournaments, with Australia and the United States sharing hosting duties.

However, Spain's ambitious bid could bring the men's tournament back to Europe for the first time since France hosted in 2023.

Some of football's most iconic stadiums could even be set for a rugby makeover.

World Rugby is looking to expand the sport's global appeal, with the next four tournaments taking place outside Europe.

The 2031 tournament will be the first men's Rugby World Cup staged in the United States, marking a major milestone for the sport.

However, European supporters hoping to watch the men's tournament closer to home must wait until at least 2035.

Spain is no stranger to hosting rugby in front of enormous crowds.

A staggering 99,124 spectators packed into Barcelona's Camp Nou to watch Racing 92 defeat Toulon in the 2016 Top 14 final.

Now, Spain wants to bring the biggest tournament in rugby to its shores.

Barcelona's Camp Nou and Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu could provide spectacular backdrops for the competition.

Spain will also be able to build on the infrastructure developed for the 2030 FIFA World Cup, which it will co-host alongside Portugal and Morocco.

The country's national rugby team has already qualified for the 2027 Rugby World Cup, ending a 28-year absence from the tournament.

With England and South Africa opting against submitting bids, Spain faces competition from two rival proposals.

- 🇪🇸 Spain: Looking to host for the first time.

- 🇯🇵 Japan: Hoping to repeat the success of 2019.

- 🌎 South America: A joint bid involving Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay.

Should Spain's bid prove unsuccessful, Europe would miss out on three successive men's Rugby World Cups.

If Japan or South America wins the race for 2035, European supporters will have to wait until at least 2039.

When will the 2035 Rugby World Cup host be confirmed?

Under World Rugby's host selection process, a preferred host is expected to be identified in May 2027, with the final decision scheduled for November.

Spain offers the opportunity to take rugby's biggest tournament into a new market while bringing it back within easy reach of millions of European supporters.

For now, Spain is flying the flag for an entire continent.
