The Australian Open starts Jan. 17 at Melbourne Park, where Sinner has had a lot of success.

He won his first Grand Slam singles title by beating Daniil Medvedev in five sets in the 2024 final, then defended it by winning the 2025 final against Zverev.

In his seven trips to the Australian Open, he has a 27-5 win-loss record for an 84% success rate. He lost in the 2026 semifinals to Novak Djokovic.

On Wednesday, the Australian Open account on X appeared to foreshadow Sinner's non-appearance in Melbourne. It issued a post which suggested Sinner might have already decided not to play in Australia in January.

"We'll miss you this summer, @janniksin. Wishing you a speedy recovery," it said.

title: Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand And Tanvi Sharma Reach Syed Modi International Finals To Keep India In Double-Title Hunt
article_text:
India will have two titles at stake on Sunday after defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, and teen sensation Tanvi Sharma, made the finals of the Syed Modi India International Super 300 badminton tournament at Lucknow on Saturday.

Top seeds Treesa and Gayatri came back from a game down to beat Ukrainian third seeds Polina Buhrova and Yevheniia Kantemyr 13-21, 21-10, 21-12 and reach their third successive final at the tournament.

They will meet Indonesian fourth seeds Isyana Syahira Meida and Rinjani Kwinnara Nastine, who beat England's Abbygael Harris and Estelle Van Leeuwen 21-13, 21-18.

Tanvi also recovered from a game down to beat compatriot Unnati Hooda 11-21, 21-10, 21-13 in an all-Indian women's singles semifinal.

The 17-year-old second seed, who won the Taipei Open Super 300 earlier this year, will face Thailand's fourth seed Supanida Katethong in the summit clash. Katethong beat top seed Riko Gunji of Japan 21-16, 20-22, 21-10 in the other semifinal.

In the mixed doubles, India's Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram and Reshika Uthayasooriyan, however, lost 17-21, 18-21 to Malaysia's Wee Yee Hern and Vannee Gobi in the semifinals.

The match between the two Indian shuttlers moved at a frenetic pace, with short and sharp rallies. Hooda kept it simple in the opening game, playing some impressive shots, while Tanvi was too erratic. Hooda raced to a 9-2 lead with a winner, and a tight net shot gave her a six-point cushion.

After the break, Hooda stretched the lead to 16-8 with some fine winners, helped by Tanvi's continued unforced errors. She earned game points with a quick follow-up at the net and sealed the game immediately with an angled drop.

Tanvi was a different player after the change of ends, opening up a 7-1 lead with her sharp stroke-play.

A service error into the net from Hooda made it 9-3, and Tanvi then unleashed a brutal smash and won a net duel to go into the interval 11-4 up.

Tanvi quickly moved to 14-5, while Hooda continued to miss her shots, twice landing wide of the lines to trail 10-19.

Another fine shot gave Tanvi 10 game points, and she levelled the match when Hooda found the net.

In the decider, Tanvi continued to dominate with her precision to lead 6-3. She moved to 9-6, and a straight smash down the line gave her a five-point advantage at the break.

It was soon 17-9 for Tanvi, who earned seven match points when Hooda found the net. She sealed the win when Hooda sprayed a shot wide.

Treesa and Gayatri fell 3-8 behind in the opening game but fought their way back to 8-9. The Ukrainians kept their noses ahead and then pulled away from 15-13 with six straight points to take the game.

The Indian pair produced a superb comeback after the change of ends, surging to 9-2. Despite a tough fight from Buhrova and Kantemyr, Treesa and Gayatri stayed in control to take the game and draw level.

They carried the momentum into the decider, dominating the rallies to jump to 9-2 before going into the break with a seven-point cushion. The Indians kept a firm grip on the match to seal their place in the final.

title: Yee Hern-Vannee one win away from second World Tour crown
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wee Yee Hern-Vannee Gobi are just one match away from claiming their second World Tour title after storming into the Syed Modi International mixed doubles final on Saturday.

The world No. 61 defeated India's world No. 185 Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram-Reshika Uthayasooriyan 21-17, 21-18 in the semi-finals at the BBD Uttar Pradesh Badminton Academy in Lucknow.

Yee Hern-Vannee captured their maiden World Tour title last month by winning the Super 100 Kaohsiung Masters in Taiwan.

They have now reached their first Super 300 final, where the Malaysians will face one of two Indonesian pairs — world No. 85 Rehan Naufal Kusharjanto-Melati Daeva Oktavianti or world No. 230 Jafar Hidayatullah-Rinjani Kwinnara Nastine — in Sunday's title showdown.

title: BMW drives Australian PGA Championship partnership into 2028
article_text:
BMW has extended its partnership with the PGA of Australia for a further two years, retaining naming rights to the BMW Australian PGA Championship through to the end of 2028.

- BMW extends its five-year partnership with the PGA of Australia, continuing as a Premier Partner into 2027 and 2028.

- This week's winner of the BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes Golf Club will, for the first time, earn an exemption into the PGA Championship major in the United States in May.

- BMW will for the first time be a Major Partner of the Australian WPGA Championship at Sanctuary Cove and the Japan-Australasia Championship in Auckland, New Zealand.

The renewal builds on a five-year relationship, with BMW continuing as a Premier Partner of the PGA of Australia.

Being contested this week in Sydney at The Lakes Golf Club, the BMW Australian PGA Championship has a history spanning more than 120 years, making it one of Australian sport's oldest and most prestigious annual events.

It is a marquee tournament on the Challenger PGA Tour of Australasia and the opening event on the DP World Tour schedule.

For the first time, this week’s winner will receive an exemption into one of golf’s four men’s majors, the PGA Championship in the United States in May.

As part of the extended partnership, BMW will for the first time be a Major Partner of the Australian WPGA Championship at Sanctuary Cove on the Gold Coast and the Japan-Australasia Championship in Auckland, New Zealand.

BMW will continue as a Major Partner with the Challenger PGA Tour of Australasia and WPGA Tour of Australasia, reflecting its ongoing commitment to supporting professional golf opportunities for both men and women.

BMW’s on-course initiatives produced another standout moment at the BMW Australian PGA Championship on Friday, when NSW professional Robbie Minns recorded a hole-in-one to win a BMW X5 40i.

PGA of Australia Chief Executive Officer Gavin Kirkman said the continuation of the BMW partnership was a significant endorsement of the organisation and the future of professional golf in Australia.

“BMW has been an outstanding partner of the PGA over the past five years, and we're delighted to continue that relationship,” Kirkman said.

“The BMW Australian PGA Championship is one of the biggest events on our calendar, and having a global brand like BMW continue its naming rights commitment is fantastic for the championship and Australian golf.

“With the championship returning to Sydney and a strong schedule of men's and women's events ahead, this partnership provides an excellent platform to continue growing the game and delivering outstanding experiences for players, fans and partners.”

BMW Group Australia Chief Executive Officer Vikram Pawah said the extension reflected BMW's confidence in the partnership and its ongoing commitment to Australian golf.

“Our partnership with the PGA of Australia has been incredibly rewarding over the past five years, and we're proud to extend that relationship into 2027 and 2028.

“The BMW Australian PGA Championship is a major fixture on the Australian sporting calendar, and its return to Sydney this week has provided an exciting opportunity to connect with golf fans in one of the country's great sporting cities.

“We're also pleased to continue supporting the broader professional game, including the WPGA Tour of Australasia and the Australian WPGA Championship. Golf has a wonderful ability to bring people together, and we're looking forward to building on what has been a successful partnership.”

title: 2026 Hero World Challenge field: PGA Tour players, rankings
article_text:
The 2026 Hero World Challenge field is set with the passing of the PGA Tour tournament entry deadline. The field is set for this FedEx Cup Fall event, played at Albany Golf Club in The Bahamas, from December 3-6, 2026.

The Hero World Challenge field is headlined by the likes of Scottie Scheffler, Tiger Woods, Matt Fitzpatrick and more. This event moves the PGA Tour to The Bahamas for the Tiger Woods-hosted Challenge event, which is unofficial but sanctioned by the PGA Tour.

This is set to be a 20-player field is played out over four days, with this event marking the final sanctioned solo tournament of the 2026 PGA Tour schedule.

The 20-player tournament is being played in its originally intended slot, offering Official World Golf Ranking points to the winner and 18 players in the field.

We do not have Monday qualifiers for this event, which will be played Thursday though Sunday.

The Hero World Challenge alternate list has already been set, with the top names at present on the list set to replace any withdrawn players.

The field will be playing for a $5 million purse, with 18 of the top 50 in the Official World Golf Ranking among the top contenders.

title: Nicolai von Dellingshausen cements lead in Sydney
article_text:
Nicolai von Dellingshausen maintained his lead at the 2027 BMW Australian PGA Championship with a third round of 69.

The German fired six birdies around The Lakes GC to ensure he will go into Sunday's final round 16 under par, holding a three-stroke lead over Alex Noren.

Von Dellingshausen said: "Overall, really happy with the score but most of all, very happy how I managed everything."

Kiradech Aphibarnrat, who narrowly missed out on full DP World Tour playing rights for this season after finishing 110th on the 2026 Race to Dubai Rankings delivered by DP World, shot 65 to share third place with Von Dellingshausen's playing partner Tom McKibbin on 12 under. First-round leader Haydn Barron was a shot further back as the leading Australian.

Von Dellinghausen had begun his tournament with three birdies in five holes on Thursday and after bogeying the 16th and 18th, responded by playing his next 34 holes in 15 under par.

That included three straight birdies to finish his opening 67, an eight-under-par 64 on Friday featuring five birdies and a stunning albatross at the 14th, and then birdies at the first, third and fifth on Saturday after some perfect approach play.

He finally dropped shots again at the eighth and tenth but bounced back immediately with a neat birdie putt at the next before adding another at the 14th.

As rain arrived late in his round - with the tee times having been moved forward around three and a half hours to between 6.50am and 8.35am local time to avoid the worst of the forecast weather in Sydney - he raised the volume at the designated 'party hole', the 15th, with a long putt for his sixth birdie of the day and 18th of the week to accompany the albatross.

Despite a dropped shot at the next, the 33-year-old - winner of the 2025 Austrian Alpine Open presented by SalzburgerLand - remained comfortably ahead of the field.

Noren birdied the fourth, fifth and eighth in an outward nine of 32 and piled on further gains at the tenth and 11th.

Two more followed at the 14th and 17th in a bogey-free round and the Swede said: “Yeah, extremely pleased. I played similar to yesterday, but probably a little bit better even today.

Aphibarnrat opened with a birdie and then poured in another five in six holes from the fifth, a sequence capped by a magnificent approach to the tenth.

Another followed at the 13th and though he bogeyed the 16th, a stunning long birdie putt at the last completed a wonderful 65.

"The putter was really hot today," acknowledged the popular Thai before speaking of his disappointment at his finish to last season.

"Like everyone knows, I really worked hard the last few years, it's never been easy.

"The last four or five events, I think I had a lot of pressure on my shoulders. In the end I got Category 18, still playing on this tour, barely.

"I think I left some pressure behind me now, I'll just go out and play my own game and hope results go my way."

Barron rediscovered the form of round one, when he had nine birdies including eight in the space of 12 holes from the sixth to the 17th.

He shot 75 in the second round but went out in 33 on Saturday with birdies at the fourth and fifth, then picked up four shots in as many holes with birdies at the 11th and 13th and an eagle at the 14th.

"Very happy with the round," he said. "Obviously a bit of a contrast from yesterday's round, just came out today with a different vibe."

Dutchman Lars van der Vight was alone in sixth on ten under with two-time champion Adam Scott nine under alongside New Zealand's Daniel Hillier and American MJ Maguire. Canada's Thomas Giroux rounded out the top ten.

title: MJ Daffue undergoing treatment on brain tumor following DP World Tour promotion
article_text:
Weeks after earning promotion to the DP World Tour, MJ Daffue ended up in the hospital with an infection.

The 37-year-old South African said doctors could not find the source but while treating him located a tumor on his brain and assigned medication aimed to attack the legion that has left him struggling a bit physically.

“Its taken a while to post anything about this year because of the difficult time the past 2 weeks has been. This year has been incredible and we have been so blessed with good golf,” Daffue wrote on Instagram.

He added the doctors found a tumor on his liver, with further scans revealing that it is benign.

“Unfortunately the one on my brain is still a mystery,” Daffue posted. “I am in great spirits and the care team and neurosurgeon has a perfect plan. I feel very confident that this is something that i will also kick butt and be ready to go soon.”

Daffue earned his first career win at the HotelPlanner Tour’s NTT Data Pro-Am on home soil in February. He proved the victory was not a fluke, following it up with a trip to the winner’s circle at the DP World PGTI Open in India a month later.

Daffue ended the season fifth on the 2026 Road to Mallorca Rankings after a solo third finish at the HotelPlanner Tour’s Grand Final in Spain earlier this month.

In addition to his work in Mallorca, his other 2026 highlights included a T-9 finish at Alfred Dunhill Links Championship in October and a T-4 placement two weeks prior at the Open de Portugal.

“I appreciate all the messages so far and cant wait to be fully healthy and attacking the top of the leaderboards again soon,” Daffue said at the end of his post. “Happy thanksgiving to everyone. Enjoy a great time with your loved ones.”

title: How an angry Jordan Spieth responded to criticism from PGA Tour pros after sponsor exemption fiasco
article_text:
Jordan Spieth was the best golfer on the planet only a decade or so ago.

After his win at the Open Championship in 2017, he had three major championships to his name, as well as 11 PGA Tour titles.

He had achieved all of that by the age of just 23. However, he has been on a steady decline ever since then.

Jordan Spieth has not added to his major tally since his triumph at Royal Birkdale and has only won two PGA Tour events over the past nine years.

In spite of that barren run, Spieth remains one of the game's biggest blockbuster stars due to his thrilling playing style.

Due to the fact that he is such a big star in the game, he receives more sponsor invites than most other players.

And many of Spieth's peers simply cannot accept that.

Back in 2025, after Spieth received sponsors' invites into five Signature Events, the three-time major champion was on the wrong end of huge criticism.

Some of his fellow pros were irked that Spieth was receiving so many exemptions.

Robert Garrigus was among those who took aim at the 33-year-old from Dallas, Texas.

"What's happening to the Tour?" he asked during an interview with Golfweek.

He added: "Tell Spieth I'll play him for any amount he wants. I win, I get his five invites to the signature events."

Spieth then responded to those digs, suggesting that the criticism he had received was completely unfair.

"It stinks. I was catching strays for no reason from guys who I had pretty good relationships with," Spieth replied.

"I'm not, like, paying tournaments to get in. There's a reason that they're going to pick me to go in. If it's going to be helpful to their tournament, then they're going to want me there, until they don't want me there."

Jordan Spieth made a great point. He is not begging the sponsors of these events to invite him to play.

The sponsors know that Jordan Spieth will sell more tickets than, for example, Robert Garrigus would.

The fact that some PGA Tour players cannot fathom that is mind-boggling. Spieth has earned the invites he receives through everything he has achieved in the game.

And the criticism he has received can't be anything more than sour grapes from his fellow pros.

title: British Cycling announce 2027 Lloyds National Mountain Bike Cross-Country and Downhill Series and Championships Calendars
article_text:
British Cycling has unveiled the 2027 Lloyds National Mountain Bike Cross-Country and Lloyds National Mountain Bike Downhill series and championships calendars, with five rounds of each series and a National Championships for both disciplines in July, bringing riders and fans to the most scenic locations and all the mud to go with it.

Five rounds of the cross-country series will be on offer, spanning the length and breadth of the country from April to June, culminating in a thrilling National Championships in July.

Five rounds of the downhill series will be on offer, bringing riders to Wales and Scotland from April to September, alongside an intense National Championships in July.
